ci: add hardened crates publish workflow

Adds a hardened crates.io publish workflow: tag-only trigger (v*), tag/version + semver validation, main ancestry check, test run, cargo-deny + cargo-audit, dry-run publish.
Add continuous monitoring watch mode for SBOM directories
Remove scripts directory and add to gitignore

Improve CLI/TUI user experience

- Fix query file detection with proper SBOM extension matching
- Show enrichment progress and failure warnings without -v flag
- Surface enrichment errors in TUI footer
- Unify output defaults to "auto" (TTY-aware) across all commands
- Rename --osv-timeout to --api-timeout for consistency
- Enable search in View mode for legacy diff TUI
- Fix 3 pre-existing clippy warnings

Add UX improvements and fix doctests

Add --fail-on-vuln for view, --dry-run for watch, export overwrite
protection, tab-specific help overlays, session tab persistence,
multi-standard SARIF, config subcommand, export filename templates,
and man page generation. Fix 4 broken doctests referencing stale APIs.

Add 8-category quality scoring engine v2.0

Expand quality scoring from 5 to 8 categories with new metrics for
hash integrity, document provenance, and component lifecycle.

- HashQualityMetrics: weak/strong classification (MD5/SHA-1 vs SHA-256+)
- DependencyMetrics: cycle detection (DFS), islands (union-find), depth (BFS)
- ProvenanceMetrics: creator, freshness, completeness declaration, signature
- LifecycleMetrics: EOL/stale/deprecated/archived counts from enrichment
- CompletenessDeclaration enum and SignatureInfo from CycloneDX parsing
- N/A-aware weight renormalization for enrichment-dependent categories
- Hard score caps: EOL→D, cycles→B, no hashes→C for Security/CRA
- TUI: 8-bar chart, integrity/provenance panels, adaptive layout
Bump version to 0.1.10

Bump MSRV to 1.88, update dependencies, fix clippy suggestions

- Bump rust-version to 1.88 to allow time crate security update
- Update time 0.3.45→0.3.47 (fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0009 stack exhaustion)
- Update 12 dependencies (aws-lc-rs, clap, darling, instability, etc.)
- Apply 164 clippy suggestions from Rust 1.88 (let-chain syntax, etc.)

Harden CI/CD pipeline and add supply chain security

- Add deny.toml for cargo-deny license/advisory/ban/source policy
- Add rust-toolchain.toml pinning Rust 1.88 with clippy+rustfmt
- Rewrite rust.yml: lint, MSRV, test matrix (3 OS), cargo-deny, CI gate
- Harden publish workflow with trusted publishing (OIDC) and cargo-deny-action
- Add release script preventing tag-before-version-bump mistakes
- Add dependabot.yml for weekly GitHub Actions and Cargo updates
- Add OSSF Scorecard workflow for supply chain visibility
- Remove non-functional SLSA placeholder workflow
- Pin all GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs
- Fix two clippy lints from Rust 1.88 (renamed lint, format args)
Apply rustfmt 1.88 formatting across codebase
Fix CI: remove --all-targets from clippy (unwrap_used in tests)
Fix CI: use MSRV toolchain for lint job (matches rust-toolchain.toml)
Fix clippy: inline format args in platform-specific code
Add security policy with vulnerability reporting guidelines

Improve OpenSSF Scorecard: add CodeQL, cargo-audit, token permissions

- Add CodeQL workflow for Rust static analysis (SAST)
- Add cargo-audit security audit job to CI pipeline
- Add top-level permissions: read-all to CI workflow (token permissions)
- Pin dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master to SHA in test matrix
- Update Cargo.lock
Fix cargo-audit: install from source instead of broken rustsec/audit-check action

Add cargo-fuzz targets for SBOM parser fuzzing

Six fuzz targets covering all parser paths:
- fuzz_parse_sbom: main entry point (format detection + all parsers)
- fuzz_cyclonedx_json: CycloneDX JSON with envelope wrapping
- fuzz_cyclonedx_xml: CycloneDX XML with envelope wrapping
- fuzz_spdx_json: SPDX JSON with envelope wrapping

- fuzz_detect_format: format detection heuristics

Includes seed corpus from test fixtures, CI workflow running weekly
and on parser changes, and gitignore entries for generated artifacts.
Smoke-tested locally: ~195K iterations/10s with zero crashes.

Improves OpenSSF Scorecard Fuzzing check.

Fix CI concurrency: only cancel in-progress on PRs, not main pushes

When multiple commits are pushed to main in quick succession (e.g.,
rapid-fire Copilot Autofix merges), cancel-in-progress cancels
intermediate CI/Fuzz runs. Scorecard then reports those commits as
unchecked, reducing CI-Tests and SAST scores from 10 to 9.

Fix: set cancel-in-progress conditionally — cancel on PRs (saves
CI minutes) but run to completion on main pushes (every commit
gets checked for Scorecard compliance).

Also tracks fuzz/Cargo.lock for reproducible fuzz builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix vulnerability score inflating quality rating when no vuln data exists (#18)

VulnerabilityMetrics::documentation_score() returned 100/100 when an SBOM
had zero vulnerability data (e.g. empty `vulnerabilities: []`), inflating
the overall quality score. This awarded a perfect score for a category
that was never actually assessed.

Change documentation_score() to return Option<f32>, returning None when
no vulnerability data exists. The scorer now treats the vulnerability
category as N/A and renormalizes weights across remaining categories,
matching the existing lifecycle_score pattern.

Before: sbom1.json scored 25.6/100 with Vulnerabilities: 100.0/100
After:  sbom1.json scores 18.6/100 with Vulnerabilities: N/A

Fixes #18

Improve graph-aware diffing: correctness, parsing, CLI config, reporting

Fix correctness bugs in graph diff (ID normalization fallback causing false
positives, edge comparison ignoring relationship/scope, reparenting suppressing
unrelated changes, cyclic nodes conflated with depth 0).

Enrich parsers: CycloneDX now infers OptionalDependsOn from scope, SPDX maps
11 additional relationship types. Add --graph-impact-threshold and
--graph-relations CLI flags. Wire --graph-diff into multi-SBOM commands.

Expand reporting with impact breakdowns in summary and detailed graph change
tables in markdown. Add 19 new unit tests (31 total) covering edge cases
like cycles, reparenting, large graphs, and relation filtering.

CRA P3.2: Annex III/IV product class + conformity-route severity calibration

Adds the CRA product-class taxonomy from Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Annex
III/IV and the matching Annex VIII conformity-assessment routes, then
threads them through `ComplianceChecker` so existing CRA findings scale
their severity per class. Backwards compatible: when no class is set,
the existing CraPhase1/CraPhase2 thresholds and severities are preserved
verbatim.

Model:
- `CraProductClass` {Default, ImportantClass1, ImportantClass2, Critical}
  with serde rename = "kebab-case" (custom names: "important-class-1",
  "important-class-2") and CLI parser (`parse_cli` accepts aliases like
  "important-1", "annex-iv", "critical").
- `ConformityRoute` {ModuleA, ModuleBC, ModuleH, Eucc} with default route
  per class (Default/Important-1 → ModuleA, Important-2 → ModuleBC,
  Critical → Eucc).
- `CraSidecarMetadata` extended with `product_class` and
  `conformity_assessment_route` fields. Sidecar value wins over CLI flag.

Compliance checker:
- `ComplianceChecker::with_product_class()` + `effective_product_class()`
  + `effective_route()` + `has_explicit_product_class()`.
- New `ClassCheck` enum + `class_severity()` mapping per the CRA-P3.2
  calibration table (vendor-hash, EOL, cycles, DoC, EUCC, PSIRT,
  attestation).
- `vendor_hash_threshold()` returns the class-specific single-stage
  threshold (Default 50%, Important-1/2 80%, Critical 100%).

Calibration applied to:
- Vendor-hash carry-through ([PRE-7-RQ-07-RE]) — class-driven threshold +
  severity.
- EOL Art. 13(8) violations — Warning at Default/Important-1, Error at
  Important-2/Critical.
- Annex VII Declaration-of-Conformity reference — Info → Warning → Error.
- Article 14 PSIRT / 24h / 72h channels — Warning at Default/Important-1,
  Error at Important-2/Critical (post-deadline only).

New checks (only fire when a product class is pinned):
- EUCC (Common Criteria) reference — Info at Important-2, Error at
  Critical. Satisfied by a Certification/Attestation external reference
  whose URL contains "eucc" or "common-criteria".
- Module-attestation reference — Warning at Important-1, Error at
  Important-2/Critical. Skipped on Module A (self-assessment).

CLI:
- `--cra-product-class {default|important-class-1|important-class-2|critical}`
  on `validate`, `quality`, and `view`.
- Mismatch between CLI flag and sidecar logs a warning; sidecar wins.
- `QualityScorer::with_cra_product_class()` mirrors the path used by
  `--profile cra` so quality scoring stays consistent with validate.

Tests: `tests/cra_product_class_tests.rs` (24 cases) covers vendor-hash
threshold ramp, severity ramp per class, EOL/DoC/EUCC/attestation
escalation, sidecar precedence, and the `class_severity` table.

CRA P3.3: Article 24 open-source software steward profile

Adds ComplianceLevel::CraOssSteward — the CRA Article 24 lighter profile
for open-source software stewards (Eclipse Foundation, Apache, Linux
Foundation, etc.). Stewards still operate under the CRA but with
reduced obligations vs. full manufacturers.

Obligation matrix:
| Check                          | Phase1/2  | OssSteward |
|--------------------------------|-----------|------------|
| SBOM completeness              | Required  | Required   |
| Vuln-handling process (Annex I)| Required  | Required   |
| CVD policy (Art. 13(7))        | Required  | Recommended (Warning) |
| Manufacturer email (Art. 13(15))| Required | NOT enforced |
| EU DoC (Annex VII)             | Required  | NOT enforced |
| Conformity-assessment module   | Required  | NOT applied |
| Article 14 reporting channels  | Required  | NOT applied |
| Hardware [PRE-8-RQ-02]         | Required  | NOT applied |
| Vendor-hash carry-through      | Required  | Recommended only |

Vulnerability-handling floor satisfied by:
- SecurityContact / Advisories / VulnerabilityAssertion external ref, OR
- sidecar `psirt_url` / `vulnerability_disclosure_url`.

CVD policy satisfied by:
- Advisories external ref, OR
- sidecar `coordinated_disclosure_policy_url`.

API:
- `ComplianceLevel::CraOssSteward` variant; `is_cra()` returns true
  (stewards are CRA-aligned), `cra_phase()` returns None.
- New `check_cra_oss_steward()` with the lighter check set.
- `CraSidecarMetadata::is_oss_steward: bool` (skip-on-default for clean
  serialisation).

CLI:
- `--standard oss-steward` (aliases: `cra-oss-steward`, `cra-oss`,
  `art24`, `cra-art24`) on the `validate` subcommand.

Tests: tests/cra_oss_steward_tests.rs (12 cases) covers the obligation
matrix above, sidecar fallbacks, and the steward-specific must-haves.

CRA P3.1: CSAF v2.0 (ISO/IEC 20153:2025) ingest

Adds a CSAF v2.0 advisory parser to VexEnricher, satisfying CRA
prEN 40000-1-3 [RLS-2-RQ-03-RE]. CSAF is the OASIS-published advisory
format named in the regulation; Red Hat, Cisco, Siemens, and Bosch all
publish CSAF advisories that include VEX-style product status. This
extends the existing OpenVEX + CycloneDX VEX paths so any of the three
formats works through `--vex` without a `--format` flag.

Auto-detection priority in VexEnricher::from_files:
1. CSAF v2.0  — `document.csaf_version` starts with "2."
2. CycloneDX VEX — `bomFormat: "CycloneDX"` + non-empty vulnerabilities
   + empty/missing components
3. OpenVEX (catch-all)

Status mapping CSAF → VexState:
- known_affected, recommended       → Affected
- known_not_affected                → NotAffected
- fixed, first_fixed, last_affected → Fixed
- under_investigation               → UnderInvestigation

Product resolution: `product_status[*]` references `product_id`s, which
are resolved against `product_tree.full_product_names[]`,
recursively-flattened `product_tree.branches[].product`, and
`product_tree.relationships[].full_product_name` for their
`product_identification_helper.purl`. Entries lacking a PURL fall back
to unscoped `vuln_id → status` so fuzzy matching can still apply.

Vuln-ID precedence: `vulnerabilities[].cve` (preferred) → first
non-empty `vulnerabilities[].ids[].text` (covers GHSA/vendor IDs).

Tests:
- 8 unit tests in src/enrichment/vex/csaf.rs covering format detection,
  parsing, branched product trees, missing-PURL fallback, vendor-ID
  fallback, and rejection of non-2.x CSAF.
- 8 integration tests in tests/csaf_tests.rs exercising the full
  VexEnricher → SBOM enrichment pipeline against two fixtures
  (`example-advisory.csaf.json`, `branched-tree.csaf.json`).

CycloneDX VEX detection tightened to require non-empty `vulnerabilities`
to avoid false positives on ordinary CycloneDX SBOMs.

CRA P5.1: populate SARIF helpUri for compliance rules + standard refs

Surfaces canonical regulation / specification URLs in two SARIF
locations so downstream GRC tooling and CI dashboards can deep-link
straight to the harmonised standard:

- `runs[].tool.driver.rules[].helpUri` (standard SARIF 2.1.0 field) —
  derived from rule-ID prefix at serialization time via a `SarifRuleWithUri`
  flatten-wrapper so the existing 70+ `SarifRule { ... }` literals stay
  unchanged.
- `runs[].results[].properties.standardHelpUris` — parallel array to the
  existing `standardIds`, carrying per-StandardRef canonical URLs.

`StandardRef::new` now auto-populates `help_uri` via
`StandardKind::canonical_help_uri()`. Stable URLs:

| Standard            | URL                                                       |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| CRA Article / Annex | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2847/oj/eng        |
| BSI TR-03183-2      | bsi.bund.de TR-03183 landing page                         |
| NIST SSDF           | doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218                           |
| EO 14028            | federalregister.gov/d/2021-10460                          |
| FDA premarket       | fda.gov cybersecurity-medical-devices guidance            |
| NTIA Minimum        | ntia.doc.gov sbom_minimum_elements_report.pdf             |
| CSAF v2.0           | docs.oasis-open.org/csaf/csaf/v2.0/csaf-v2.0.html         |
| CNSA 2.0            | media.defense.gov CSA_CNSA_2.0_ALGORITHMS_.PDF            |
| NIST PQC            | csrc.nist.gov/projects/post-quantum-cryptography          |

prEN 40000-1-3 returns None — the draft EN is paywalled and CEN URLs
are unstable; will revisit when the standard is finalised.

URLs are root-of-standard, not per-clause anchors — EUR-Lex and most
national bodies don't publish stable per-article fragments. Per-clause
precision lives in `StandardRef::id` (e.g., "Art. 13(4)") and
`Violation::requirement`.

Tests: tests/sarif_help_uri_tests.rs (8 cases) covers
canonical_help_uri()'s coverage, prEN/Other → None, SARIF rule helpUri
emission for CRA + BSI, and `properties.standardHelpUris` on results.

CRA P4.2: CSAF v2.0 advisory emitter + `vex export` CLI

Closes the round-trip with P3.1 ingest: an SBOM whose vulnerabilities
carry VexStatus values can now be exported as a CSAF v2.0 advisory
that re-ingests cleanly back into the same VEX state.

CLI:
  sbom-tools vex export <sbom> [--vex <path>...] [--format csaf] [-O <file>]

`--format csaf` (default) emits a `csaf_vex` document; CSAF aliases
`csaf-v2.0`, `csaf2` are accepted. Other advisory formats (OpenVEX
emit, CycloneDX VEX emit) can slot into `VexExportFormat` later.

Mapping internal model → CSAF v2.0:

| Internal                           | CSAF v2.0                                    |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Component with PURL                | product_tree.full_product_names[].purl       |
| `VexState::Affected`               | product_status.known_affected[]              |
| `VexState::NotAffected`            | product_status.known_not_affected[]          |
| `VexState::Fixed`                  | product_status.fixed[]                       |
| `VexState::UnderInvestigation`     | product_status.under_investigation[]         |
| `Vulnerability.id` starting "CVE-" | vulnerabilities[].cve                        |
| Other vuln IDs (GHSA-, RUSTSEC-, …)| vulnerabilities[].ids[].text + system_name   |

Document metadata defaults:
- category: `csaf_vex`
- publisher: organization creator from SBOM, else `sbom-tools`
- title: `VEX advisory for <document.name|primary>`
- tracking.id: `sbom-tools-vex-<UTC timestamp>`
- generator.engine: `sbom-tools <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>`
All overridable via `CsafEmitOptions`.

Components without a PURL are skipped (no resolvable identifier in
CSAF's product_tree).

Tests:
- 4 unit tests in `src/reports/csaf.rs` (skeleton, state grouping,
  GHSA fallback, no-PURL skip).
- 5 integration tests in `tests/csaf_emit_tests.rs` including:
  - `round_trip_preserves_vex_states_across_ingest_emit_ingest` —
    parses the canonical fixture, enriches an SBOM, emits CSAF,
    re-ingests, asserts identical (purl, vuln, state) tuples.
  - `emitted_csaf_passes_internal_format_detector` — ensures the
    emitter output is auto-detected as CSAF (not OpenVEX/CDX-VEX).

CRA audit fixes: TUI sidecar plumbing + cra-docs section numbering

End-to-end audit of CLI + TUI surfaces uncovered two gaps:

1. **TUI compliance tab ignored the CRA sidecar.** The compliance tab's
   `compute_compliance_results()` instantiated `ComplianceChecker::new()`
   without `with_sidecar()`, so OSS-Steward, EUCC, Article 14, and
   product-class-conditional checks all rendered as if no sidecar had
   been supplied — a TUI user with `productClass=critical` and a fully
   populated sidecar would still see 4 spurious EUCC errors and miss
   the conformity-summary line.

   Fix: added `ViewApp::with_cra_sidecar()` builder + an
   `Option<CraSidecarMetadata>` field on `ViewApp`. `cli/view.rs` now
   resolves the sidecar (explicit `--cra-sidecar` → auto-discover) and
   feeds it into the TUI before launching `run_view_tui`.
   `compute_compliance_results()` takes the sidecar and threads it
   into every per-level `ComplianceChecker`.

2. **cra-docs labelled both extra sections as `## 8`.** When both the
   prEN 40000-1-2/1-4 controls-assertion block and the NIS2/GDPR/AI
   Act/RED adjacent-regulation block were present, the dossier
   produced two consecutive headings numbered "## 8". Fixed by
   bumping adjacent-regulation to "## 9". When only one of the two
   sections fires, "## 8" or "## 9" appears alone (cosmetic gap, not a
   collision).

Audit verified end-to-end smoke tests of:
- `validate --standard {cra,bsi,oss-steward,eucc}` — all four exit cleanly
- `validate --standard cra,bsi,oss-steward` — multi-standard JSON output
- `validate --cra-product-class important-class-2` — class mismatch warns,
  sidecar wins; conformity_summary populates in JSON output
- `quality --profile cra --cra-product-class critical` — score adjusts
- `cra-docs <sbom> --output <dir> --cra-sidecar <full-sidecar>` — produces
  9-section dossier with controls-assertion + adjacent-regulation
- `cra-standards-watch` (table + json) — curated catalogue prints cleanly
- `vex export --format csaf` → `vex apply` — round-trip clean
- SARIF helpUri populated on every CRA rule + result

Fix semantic similarity percentage overflow (#188)

* fix(diff): bound semantic similarity score

* style(diff): format similarity regressions

* refactor(diff): document normalize_semantic_score and loosen test tolerance

- extract PERCENT_MAX = 100.0 constant; reuse it in both the identical-hash
  fast path and the budget-based normalization to keep the percent ceiling
  in one place
- doc-comment normalize_semantic_score explaining the upper-bound budget
  per axis, the modified.len() choice, and why vulnerability_resolved is
  intentionally absent from the budget (it is a reward in CostModel, not a
  cost, so it can only reduce raw_cost and never violate the bound)
- loosen the direction-independence assertion in
  compute_diff_similarity_is_bounded_in_both_directions from f64::EPSILON
  (~2.2e-16) to 1e-9; the EPSILON tolerance only passed today because the
  forward and reverse paths produce bit-identical f64 results, which is
  fragile against any future reordering of the budget arithmetic. The 1e-9
  tolerance still catches any genuine direction-dependent skew.

chore(ci): make SHA-pin version comments inline + correct, expand Dependabot coverage (#202)

The repo annotates SHA-pinned actions with a version comment on the line
*above* `uses:` — a style Dependabot cannot maintain (it only rewrites
inline same-line comments). Every action bump therefore silently drifted
the annotation. After the recent checkout 6.0.2→6.0.3 bump, 9 `# v6.0.2`
comments were left sitting above the 6.0.3 SHA, actively misrepresenting it.

Workflow hygiene (no behavioral change to which SHA runs, except the re-pin below):
- Migrate all 53 SHA-pin annotations to inline `# vX.Y.Z` so future
  Dependabot bumps self-correct.
- Correct every stale/wrong comment against the actual pinned SHA, resolved
  via the GitHub tags API:
    checkout            → v6.0.3 (was v6.0.2, ×9 stale + 8 unannotated)
    upload-artifact     → v7.0.1 (was v4 / v6.0.0 — both wrong)
    download-artifact   → v8.0.1 (was v4)
    codeql-action       → v4.36.1 (scorecard said v3 — wrong)
    cosign-installer    → v4.1.2 (was v4.1.0)
    rust-cache          → v2.9.1 (was v2 / v2.8.2)
    cargo-deny-action   → v2.0.20, scorecard-action → v2.4.3,
    setup-go → v6.4.0, attest-build-provenance → v4.1.0
    rust-toolchain      → # master (no semver releases; toolchain set via input)
- bindings.yml: annotate all 12 previously-unannotated pins.

Security re-pin:
- rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action was pinned to an unreleased `main` HEAD
  commit (1d2b8f3, 2026-05-18), 85 commits ahead of the latest release and
  mislabeled `# v1` (no `v1` tag exists). Re-pin to the v1.0.4 release SHA
  in the credentialed crates.io publish path.

Dependabot config:
- Add coverage for two previously-unmonitored manifests: the independent
  `fuzz/` Cargo workspace and the `bindings/go` Go module.
- Group minor/patch updates per ecosystem (majors stay separate) to cut
  per-update PR/CI churn.
- Add a 5-day cooldown on cargo entries, consistent open-PR limits, and
  triage labels (created the missing github-actions/go/ci/fuzzing labels).

The SLSA generator reusable workflow stays tag-pinned (@v2.1.0) by design.

fix(reports,tui): CSV formula-injection guard, terminal sanitization, TUI panic hook (#213)

Three security-hygiene gaps when rendering untrusted SBOM data
(SECURITY.md scopes untrusted SBOM inputs):

1. CSV formula injection: escape_csv only doubled quotes, so a component
   name or version like "=cmd|..." would execute as a formula when the
   CSV is opened in a spreadsheet. Cells starting with '=', '+', '-',
   '@', tab, or CR are now prefixed with a single quote per OWASP CSV
   injection guidance. String-typed cells that previously bypassed
   escaping entirely (versions, PURLs, ecosystems, algorithm family)
   are now routed through escape_csv via a new escape_csv_opt helper;
   numeric cells are formatted separately and remain untouched.

2. Terminal output sanitization: SummaryReporter and TableReporter
   interpolated component names, versions, vuln ids/severities, license
   strings, and document names into TTY output with no control-char
   stripping, letting a crafted SBOM emit ANSI escape sequences (cursor
   movement, screen clearing, title changes) or raw control characters.
   New reports::escape::sanitize_terminal strips C0 controls (except
   \n and \t), DEL, and C1 controls -- including ESC -- and is applied
   at every user-data interpolation point in both reporters.

3. TUI panic hook: enable_raw_mode + EnterAlternateScreen ran with no
   panic hook, so any panic left the shell in raw mode with the
   backtrace swallowed by the alternate screen. tui::shared now provides
   install_panic_hook (Once-guarded, chains the previous hook) and an
   idempotent restore_terminal; both run_tui and run_view_tui install it
   before entering raw mode.

fix(license): conflict gating, concluded licenses, SPDX-expression-aware policy (#212)

Four defects in the license policy engine:

- Conflict violations were pushed with PolicyDecision::Denied but
  denied_count was never incremented, so result.passed stayed true and
  fail_on_conflict was a no-op (the CLI exit code keys on denied_count).
  The conflict check is now folded into the per-component loop and marks
  the component denied, counted at most once per component.
- Only declared licenses were evaluated, so components with only a
  concluded license bypassed the deny list. Policy evaluation now
  iterates LicenseInfo::all_licenses() (declared + concluded), and
  has_conflicts() also considers the concluded license.
- matches_pattern treated a whole SPDX expression as a single ID, so
  deny "GPL-*" missed "MIT OR GPL-3.0-only" while incorrectly denying
  expressions where the licensee could choose a non-denied branch.
  evaluate_expression now parses the expression (LAX mode, matching
  model/license.rs) and uses spdx::Expression::evaluate per operand:
  OR is the licensee's choice, AND requires all operands to comply, and
  WITH exceptions match against the base license ID. Non-parseable
  expressions keep the previous whole-string fallback, and glob prefix
  matching is now case-insensitive like exact matching.
- Propagation analysis classified components by declared.first() only,
  missing copyleft in a second declared license or in the concluded
  license. It now uses the new LicenseInfo::effective_family(), which
  folds all expressions with most-restrictive-wins precedence.

fix(diff): incremental cache splices only from the last diffed pair; propagate errors (#217)

Root cause: find_previous_result selected the cached entry with the highest
hit_count, but hit_count was set to 0 at insert and never incremented, so an
arbitrary cached entry (possibly from a different SBOM pair) became the splice
base for diff_sections. Section change detection is computed against the last
diffed pair's hashes, so any other pair's entry is an invalid base and leaves
stale unchanged-sections in the output. The lookup also hardcoded a 1-hour TTL
instead of the configured cache TTL, and diff() swallowed engine errors via
unwrap_or_default(), turning failures into empty "no changes" results.

Fix:
- Track the last diffed pair as LastDiffMeta { key, old_hashes, new_hashes }
  and look up the splice base in the cache by that exact key, validated
  against the configured TTL. Evicted/expired entries fall back to a full
  computation.
- IncrementalDiffEngine::diff now returns Result<IncrementalDiffResult,
  SbomDiffError>, propagating engine.diff errors instead of defaulting; the
  fall-back-to-full-diff behavior on diff_sections errors is preserved.
- DiffCache::get increments hit_count on valid hits so the field is truthful.
- MultiDiffEngine::{diff_multi, timeline, matrix} and CLI call sites updated
  for the new Result signatures.

Partial-cache reuse becomes rarer by design (only the exact last pair
qualifies) — correctness over speed. The full-result cache is untouched.

fix(enrichment): hydrate OSV querybatch results with full vulnerability details (#219)

records were cached for 24 hours, masking the problem on subsequent

  successfully, so transient per-vuln failures are retried on the next
  run instead of pinning id-only stubs for 24 hours. Failed hydrations
  keep the id-only stub so findings are never silently dropped.

  strings (the format OSV actually returns) per the FIRST CVSS v3.1
  specification section 7.1, including the Appendix A Roundup function.
  GHSA/Ubuntu-style database_specific severity labels are used as a
  severity fallback when no CVSS entry is parseable.

fix(quality): iterative Tarjan SCC cycle detection prevents stack-overflow abort (#215)

* fix(quality): iterative Tarjan SCC cycle detection prevents stack-overflow abort

detect_cycles used a recursive DFS, so a deep dependency chain (40K-node
linear chain) overflowed the call stack and aborted the process. The
function is reachable from every QualityScorer::score call (CLI quality,
diff pipeline, TUI) and from the FFI entry sbom_tools_score_sbom_json,
where catch_unwind cannot contain a stack-overflow abort - a single
hostile SBOM could kill an embedding Go/Swift host. The recursive DFS
also counted back edges rather than cycles, so one strongly connected
component with k back edges was penalized k times (5 pts each) and any
back edge triggered the B-grade hard cap.

Replace the recursion with an iterative Tarjan SCC algorithm using
explicit stacks. cycle_count now means: number of SCCs with more than
one node, plus single-node SCCs with a self-loop. Raise
MAX_EDGES_FOR_GRAPH_ANALYSIS from 50K to 1M - it remains purely a DoS
ceiling now that recursion depth is no longer a risk. Bump
SCORING_ENGINE_VERSION to 2.1 since scores change for cyclic graphs.

Add unit tests for the 40K chain, diamond DAG, multi-back-edge SCC, and
self-loop semantics; an end-to-end deep-chain QualityScorer test; an FFI
regression test scoring a 40K-component chain; and a fuzz_score_sbom
fuzz target (parse arbitrary bytes, score with all profiles) registered
in fuzz/Cargo.toml and the fuzz workflow.

fix(matching): deterministic MinHash seeds and solver ordering; add diff property tests (#218)

Diffs of SBOMs above the 500-component LSH threshold were not
reproducible across runs, undermining CI --fail-on-* gating. Root
causes:

- LshIndex::new seeded MinHash coefficients from RandomState, so LSH
  candidate sets differed per process. Coefficients are now generated
  from a fixed seed via an inline splitmix64 PRNG (dependency-free),
  preserving the odd-multiplier coefficient property.
- optimal_assignment collected old_ids/new_ids from HashSet iteration,
  randomizing assignment-solver tie-breaking. IDs are now sorted before
  building the assignment problem, and greedy assignment breaks score
  ties by ID.

Additional nondeterminism uncovered by the new round-trip property test
(diff twice, compare serialized JSON) and fixed alongside:

- LshIndex::find_candidates_by_signature returned HashSet iteration
  order, so downstream take()-truncation selected differing subsets.
  Candidates are now returned in deterministic band/bucket order.
- ComponentIndex::find_candidates iterated the by_prefix HashMap
  (priority 3) and broke trigram-overlap ties (priority 4) in random
  order; both are now deterministic.
- ComponentChangeComputer emitted removed/modified, and
  LicenseChangeComputer emitted license changes, in match-map/HashMap
  iteration order; outputs are now sorted.
- VulnerabilityChangeSet::sort_by_severity left equal-severity entries
  (and persistent/vex_changes entirely) in HashMap order; ties now
  break by vulnerability and component ID.
- Match-metric average summed f64 scores in HashMap order; scores are
  sorted first so float accumulation is bit-identical.

reuse the arb_component strategy from proptest_matching.rs and verify:
diff(a,a) is empty; diff(a,b).added equals diff(b,a).removed by

perf(tui): cache ViewApp dependency graph and use iterative longest-path (#223)

ViewApp's Dependencies tab rebuilt the entire dependency graph on every
draw (cloning all component names/edges) even though `app.sbom` is
immutable in view mode, and the view redraws on every ~100ms idle tick.
Worse, `calculate_max_depth`'s inner `depth_of` removed nodes from
`visited` on exit, so it enumerated ALL simple paths — exponential on
diamond-heavy DAGs — and its recursion depth equaled the longest chain,
a stack-overflow hazard on deep graphs (same class as the detect_cycles
bug fixed in #215).

Fix:
- Cache the graph lazily in `DependencyViewState::cached_graph`
  (Option<DependencyGraph>), built on first Dependencies-tab render. No
  hash-keyed invalidation is needed because `app.sbom` never changes in
  view mode; the search filter only affects the separately-cached
  flattened node list. (src/tui/view/views/dependencies.rs render path,
  src/tui/view/app.rs DependencyViewState)
- Replace the recursive `depth_of` with an iterative Kahn topological
  pass + memoized per-node depth. Nodes still in a cycle after the queue
  drains keep depth 0, a well-defined stable metric replacing the old
  traversal-order-dependent recursive value. No recursion, no path
  enumeration: linear in nodes+edges.

Tests (src/tui/view/views/dependencies.rs): a 50-layer diamond lattice
(2^50 simple paths — instant now, previously exponential) and a 40K-node
linear chain (previously recursion-bound stack overflow — now completes),
plus chain/single-node/cycle-semantics coverage.

feat(config): wire the global --config flag into command execution (#227)

Root cause: ~2.4K LOC of config infrastructure (AppConfig, presets,
merge, Validatable, schema) was dead in the execution path — consumed
only by `config show/path`. The global --config flag affected no
subcommand; every command built its config purely from CLI args.
`AppConfig::from_file_with_overrides` had zero callers and the entire
validation.rs was never invoked from main/cli.

Fix:
- New binary-local `cli_config` module. `EffectiveConfig::load` discovers,
  parses, and validates the config file once in the dispatch prologue.
  Consuming commands get a strict load (parse + validation errors are hard
  errors so a broken file never silently changes behaviour); meta commands
  (config/completions/man/config-schema) get a lenient load so they are
  never blocked by an unrelated invalid config.
- Per-command config construction (Diff, View, DiffMulti, Timeline, Matrix,
  Quality, Watch) is now seeded from the loaded AppConfig as the base layer.
  Precedence: explicit CLI flag > config file value > built-in default.
  CLI explicitness is detected at the clap layer via ValueSource, so an
  explicit flag whose value equals the default (e.g. `--output auto`) still
  overrides the file while an unset flag falls through to the file value.
- Fixed the merge() sentinel-comparison bugs in config/file.rs (fuzzy_preset
  vs Balanced @181, output.format vs Auto @192, tui.theme vs Dark @261):
  the inlined literal sentinels could drift from the real default. They now
  compare against Self::default() field-by-field, read dynamically.
- Added global --no-config flag (skips discovery) and a `config check`
  action that loads + validates + prints the effective merged config.

Evidence: with `output.format: Json` in the file, `diff a b` (no -o, non-TTY
where auto resolves to summary) now emits JSON; `diff a b -o summary`
overrides it back to summary; `--no-config` ignores the file. Invalid
config (threshold 5.0) fails `config check` naming `matching.threshold`.

perf(diff): sparse assignment solver + trigram-ranked candidates (#232)

Problem: cross-format / regenerated-bom-ref diffs push nearly every
component into fuzzy assignment, yet optimal_assignment built a DENSE
n×n cost matrix and ran pathfinding's kuhn_munkres_min whenever
n <= hungarian_threshold (5000). At that boundary the matrix is ~25M
i64 entries (~200MB) and kuhn_munkres is O(n³) (~10^11 ops) — an
effective hang — even though candidates are sparse (≤~100 per source).
See the old src/diff/engine_matching.rs hungarian_assignment building
weights: Vec<Vec<i64>> over (0..n)×(0..n).

Fix:
- Replace the dense Hungarian + greedy_with_swaps/greedy fallback split
  with a single sparse solver (src/diff/engine_matching.rs
  sparse_assignment): successive shortest augmenting paths (Dijkstra
  with dual potentials) over per-source candidate adjacency lists. No
  n×n matrix is materialized; cost scales with the candidate edge count.
  Scores map to non-negative integer costs (SCALE − score·SCALE) plus a
  per-source dummy "leave unmatched" object, giving an exact min-cost
  perfect matching that recovers max-weight behavior. A reused
  touched-object scratch list keeps the settle scan / potential update
  proportional to reachable objects, not num_obj. Optimality verified by
  a greedy-trap unit test (greedy total 1.05 vs optimal 1.70). In-tree,
  no solver crate added; pathfinding dependency dropped from Cargo.toml.
- hungarian_threshold / enable_swap_optimization / max_swap_iterations
  and the unused AssignmentMethod enum removed from
  src/diff/engine_config.rs (grep confirmed nothing external set them;
  benches spread ..LargeSbomConfig::default()).
- Determinism preserved (keeps #218): old/new IDs indexed in sorted
  value order, adjacency object-index sorted, path ties break by lowest
  object index; proptest_diff large_diff_output_is_deterministic and
  proptest_matching symmetry still pass.
- Rank ComponentIndex Priority-1 same-ecosystem candidates by trigram
  overlap before truncate(max_candidates) (src/matching/index.rs) so the
  true match survives when an ecosystem bucket exceeds max_candidates.

Tests/bench:
- 5 sparse-solver unit tests (one-to-one, greedy-trap optimum,
  asymmetric more-sources-than-objects, determinism vs input order).
- integration_tests: a 400-component disjoint-canonical-id diff that
  completes fast and matches ≥380 as modified; a trigram-ranking test
  that surfaces the true match in an oversized (251) ecosystem bucket
  (verified it fails without the index.rs change).
- benches/diff_benchmark.rs: deterministic disjoint-id pair at 2k/4k
  with lsh_threshold raised so the former dense-matrix path runs; locally
  4000 dropped from 24.8s (dense) to 12.8s (sparse).

  was hand-maintained, which already caused the AiReadiness drift fixed in
  #216. Hand edits can silently desync from src/ffi.rs.

  is 0.1.21, and its path dependency on the root crate had no `version` key,
  so `cargo publish -p sbom-tools-ffi` fails (crates.io rejects versionless
  path deps). scripts/release.sh only bumped the root manifest.

- Add crates/sbom-tools-ffi/cbindgen.toml + scripts/gen-ffi-header.sh that
  regenerate the committed header from src/ffi.rs. cbindgen >= 0.29 is
  required: earlier versions do not recognise the edition-2024
  `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` attribute and drop every exported function. The
  config scopes output to the ABI surface (item_types enums/structs/functions
  + include list) so unrelated top-level `pub const`s are not emitted. The
  header is committed so offline Go/Swift consumers build without cbindgen.

  the header and `git diff --exit-code`s it, failing on drift. This is
  stronger than and complements #216's check-binding-constants.sh (which
  validates the Go/Swift wrappers, not the header itself).
- Bump crates/sbom-tools-ffi/Cargo.toml version 0.1.17 -> 0.1.21 and add
  `version = "=0.1.21"` to its sbom-tools path dep; extend scripts/release.sh
  (release.sh:99-108) to bump both manifests and the `=` pin in lockstep.

  SBOM_TOOLS_PROFILE_* while keeping the consumer-referenced type names
  SbomToolsErrorCode / SbomToolsScoringProfile. Per the deviation clause, the
  header now uses cbindgen's deterministic names SBOM_TOOLS_ERROR_CODE_* and
  SBOM_TOOLS_SCORING_PROFILE_*. Enum integer values, type names, struct layout
  and all 7 function signatures are byte-for-byte preserved. The three
  consumers were updated to the new macro spellings (Go: bindings/go/sbomtools.go;
  Swift: bindings/swift/Sources/SbomTools/SbomTools.swift; parity regex:

perf(pipeline): in-place enrichment mutation + lazy report compliance (#236)

Two separable allocation/compute wins on the shared enrichment + report path.

(a) In-place enrichment — src/pipeline/parse.rs

enrich_sbom (OSV), enrich_eol, and enrich_staleness each ran
`sbom.components.values().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>()` — a full deep clone
of every Component (each carries Vecs of vulns/hashes/refs + several Strings)
— then re-inserted the enriched copies key-by-key, rehashing the whole map.
On a large SBOM that doubled peak memory per enrichment pass and cloned the
entire component set up to three times (OSV + EOL + staleness).

Added a shared `enrich_components_in_place` helper (parse.rs:188) that
`mem::take`s the IndexMap, `unzip`s it into a keys vec + a `&mut [Component]`
slice the enricher mutates in place, then re-zips the original keys back —
values are moved, never cloned, and keys are never cloned. The enrichers only
populate vulnerabilities/eol/staleness (never canonical_id), so the
key↔value pairing is preserved by index. Behavior is identical.

(b) Lazy report compliance — src/pipeline/report_stage.rs

output_report unconditionally ran ComplianceChecker (CRA Phase 2) on BOTH
SBOMs for every format, even though only Markdown/HTML/non-streaming-JSON/
SARIF render the result (grep cra_compliance in src/reports/: summary, table,
csv, side-by-side, ndjson, and the StreamingJsonReporter never read it).
Added `format_uses_compliance` (report_stage.rs:96) and gated the two checks
behind it (and behind `!use_streaming`). Consuming reporters already fall back
to `unwrap_or_else(|| ComplianceChecker::new(..).check(sbom))` when the field
is None, so output is unchanged for every format — non-consumers just skip the
wasted O(V+E) work.

Tests: parse.rs gains a multi-component test asserting vulns land on the right
components after the in-place move-out/write-back (and that each key still maps
to its own canonical_id); report_stage.rs gains a predicate test plus a test
that the Summary reporter renders byte-identically with vs without precomputed
compliance. Full suite (898 lib + integration incl. CRA golden/readiness) green
on 1.88; 0 new clippy warnings; no new dependencies.

feat(enrichment): offline mode + cache management subcommand (#238)

Problem: the air-gapped environments sbom-tools targets (CRA/FDA/defense)
could not run enrichment without a network. A live OSV health check
(pipeline/parse.rs is_available) gated enrichment even with a warm cache;
JsonCache::get_named evicts TTL-expired entries on read so there was no
stale-if-offline fallback; EolEnricher::new fetched the product list at
construction so it could not be built offline; and there was no --offline
flag or any cache management.

Fix:
- Global --offline flag + SBOM_TOOLS_OFFLINE env (main.rs), resolved once
  and pushed into a process-wide switch (enrichment/source.rs set_offline).
  EnrichmentConfig gains an `offline` field threaded via seed_enrichment.
- HTTP layer refuses network calls when offline: get_with_retry and every
  source's direct .send() call an offline_guard() that returns a clear
  "offline: not in cache" error (EnrichmentErrorKind::Offline,
  EnrichmentError::Offline) before any socket is opened
  (osv/client.rs, eol/client.rs, kev/client.rs, staleness/registry.rs).
  The OSV is_available() health probe is skipped offline (pipeline/parse.rs)
  so cache-served enrichment proceeds.
- Stale-if-offline cache semantics: JsonCache::get_named_allow_stale returns
  a TTL-expired entry with an age signal instead of evicting it when offline;
  get_named logs a "N day(s) past TTL" warning. The online path is
  byte-identical (still evicts on read) — the E1 cache tests pass unchanged
  (source.rs ttl_expiry_evicts_entry, enrichment_http_tests.rs).
- EolEnricher::new degrades gracefully offline: a missing product list is
  served from cache or falls back to an empty list (skip) instead of failing.
- New `cache` subcommand (cli/cache.rs): status (sources, counts, ages,
  size), warm <sbom> [--all-sources] (pre-fetch so a later --offline run is
  served), clear, and export/import via a portable recursive directory copy
  (no new dependency; the cache is already a tree of small JSON files).

httpmock hits; offline cache miss makes no request; expired-entry-served-

fix(convert): preserve typed AI fields on emit; harden verify --model-dir paths (#247)

Two pre-release defects in the AI-BOM path.

1) MAJOR — emit_model_card (src/serialization/emit/cyclonedx.rs) dropped the
typed MlModel.{fairness, ethical_considerations, use_cases,
performance_metrics} fields. The CycloneDX parser populates these from a
modelCard, but the emitter only re-emitted modelParameters +
considerations.{technicalLimitations, environmentalConsiderations}. A
CycloneDX ML-BOM round-tripped through `convert --to cyclonedx` therefore
lost the data that AI-004/005/007/009 score, flipping them pass->fail and
regressing AI-readiness by ~37.5pt — violating the module invariant that
converting an AI-BOM does not regress AI scoring.

Fix: also synthesize considerations.fairnessAssessments,
considerations.ethicalConsiderations, considerations.useCases, and
modelCard.quantitativeAnalysis.performanceMetrics using the exact spec field
names/shapes the CycloneDX parser reads (CdxFairnessObj { groupAtRisk,
benefits, harms, mitigationStrategy }, CdxEthicalObj { name,
mitigationStrategy }, useCases string array, CdxPerformanceMetric { type,
value, slice }), so the typed path round-trips on its own (no --preserve
needed). The extensions.raw bridge fallback is left untouched.

SPDX side: the only SPDX emitter is SPDX 2.3, which has no AI/ML profile and
already drops ALL ml_model metadata honestly via note_unmappable; there is
no SPDX 3.0 emitter, so there is no equivalent typed-AI gap to fix.

2) SECURITY — verify --model-dir (src/verification/model_dir.rs) followed
symlinks out of the model directory. FileIndex::build resolved entries with
fs::metadata (follows symlinks) and indexed the symlink path, so a crafted
`model.safetensors -> /etc/passwd` (or `../secret`) symlink made the verifier
read an arbitrary file outside the audited tree.

Fix: canonicalize the model-dir root, canonicalize each candidate path, and
skip any whose resolved path escapes the root (FileIndex::build), storing the
bounded resolved path for the hash read. Added a visited-dir set to stay
robust against intra-tree symlinked-directory cycles. HF cache layouts
(sha256-named blobs, snapshots->blobs symlinks that stay under root) keep
working.

Regression tests:
- tests/convert_emit_tests.rs::ai_bom_convert_preserves_typed_ai_readiness_score
  parses aibom-complete.cdx.json, scores AiReadiness, converts to cyclonedx,
  re-parses, re-scores, and asserts AI-004/005/007/009 still pass and the
  overall score does not drop >2pt. Verified to FAIL without the emitter fix.
- src/verification/model_dir.rs::does_not_follow_symlink_escaping_model_dir
  proves an escaping symlink is not followed; follows_intra_tree_symlink_like_hf_cache
  proves in-tree HF symlinks still verify. The escape test was verified to FAIL
  with the guard disabled.

fix(enrichment): official EPSS endpoint, cache namespace coverage, response size bound (#248)

Three verified pre-release defects in the enrichment/cache surface.

1. Default EPSS endpoint was a non-FIRST third-party mirror.
   EPSS_SCORES_URL hardcoded https://epss.cybersecurity.fr/... and
   EpssClientConfig::default() used it, so the default `--epss` run
   fetched exploit-risk gating data from an unofficial host. Switch the
   default to the official FIRST endpoint
   https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz, which
   302-redirects to the dated .csv.gz (reqwest follows redirects). The
   payload is gzip; EpssClient::fetch_from_api now detects the gzip magic
   (0x1f 0x8b) and decompresses, while a plain body (the --epss-url /
   SBOM_TOOLS_EPSS_URL test seam) is passed through unchanged — one fetch
   path for both. Adds the flate2 crate (MIT/Apache, cargo-deny-clean) and
   pins the default host via EPSS_OFFICIAL_HOST + a regression test so it
   cannot silently drift again.
   src/enrichment/epss/client.rs:13-159, src/enrichment/epss/mod.rs, Cargo.toml

2. `cache clear`/`status` ignored the epss + huggingface namespaces.
   SOURCE_NAMESPACES omitted them, yet both clients write under
   namespaced_cache_dir("epss")/("huggingface"), so those caches were
   never purged or reported. SOURCE_NAMESPACES now lists all six.
   src/cli/cache.rs:66

3. `cache warm --all` skipped EPSS.
   cache_warm set enable_eol/kev/staleness/huggingface but not
   enable_epss (default false), so a later `--epss --offline` run could
   not be served. Sets enable_epss = all_sources and includes EPSS in the
   warm summary.
   src/cli/cache.rs:182, :199

4. No response-size bound on EPSS/KEV/HuggingFace reads.
   These buffered full bodies (response.text()/.json()) with no cap, so a
   malicious/MITM endpoint could OOM the process. Adds read_bounded in
   source.rs enforcing MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (256 MiB) against both
   Content-Length and the actually-buffered length; EPSS/KEV/HF decode the
   bounded buffer.
   src/enrichment/source.rs:163-220, kev/client.rs, huggingface/client.rs

Regression tests: default host == epss.empiricalsecurity.com; gzip
round-trip parses (unit + httpmock integration); plain body still parses;
read_bounded rejects an over-cap body and accepts a within-cap body;
SOURCE_NAMESPACES + clear logic cover epss/huggingface.

fix(cli): route enrich/watch/query through the unified enrichment orchestrator (#249)

Parallel PRs added KEV/EPSS/HuggingFace/staleness sources and the canonical
orchestrator (pipeline::enrich_sbom_full), but several entry points still
hand-rolled enrichment, so their advertised flags silently no-op'd — and one
path could re-enable network egress in an air-gapped run.

Root causes + fixes:

1. enrich silently dropped --kev/--epss/--enrich-staleness/--huggingface:
   run_enrich (src/cli/enrich.rs) only applied OSV/EOL/VEX; the four enable_*
   fields were parsed but never read. Replaced the hand-rolled blocks with a
   single enrich_sbom_full() call, which also makes enrich honor the config
   file's enrichment: block.

2. watch --huggingface was accepted but never ran HF: enrich_watched_sbom
   (src/watch/loop_impl.rs) orchestrated OSV/KEV/EPSS/EOL/staleness/VEX but had
   no HuggingFace dispatch. Added an enable_huggingface block mirroring
   enrich_sbom_full (lower-risk than delegating, which would lose watch's
   per-source bypass_cache override for periodic cycles).

3. query --offline re-enabled network egress (BLOCKER): the Query arm built
   enrichment via to_enrichment_config() which never set .offline, then
   enrich_sbom_full's unconditional set_offline(config.offline=false) overwrote
   the global offline=true that main.rs set, so the offline_guard permitted
   network calls. Fixed both layers: (a) the Query arm now routes through
   seed_enrichment (which folds in `offline`), and (b) DEFENSIVE —
   enrich_sbom_full now calls set_offline(is_offline() || config.offline) so no
   caller can ever clear a globally-set offline (src/pipeline/enrich.rs:85).

4. query ignored the global --config file: the Query arm used raw args with no
   ValueSource precedence (PR #227 migrated every other command but not Query).
   It now builds enrichment via seed_enrichment and resolves output format +
   no_color through the same resolve()/arg_was_set_sub machinery as Diff/View.

5. enrich_sbom_json (src/serialization/enricher.rs) dropped KEV/EPSS overlays on
   serialization, so even a wired-up enrich --kev wrote nothing observable.
   Now emits sbom-tools:kev / sbom-tools:epss:score CycloneDX vuln properties.

6. README exit-code table omitted code 6 (KEV_INTRODUCED), contradicting CLI
   help; added.

Regression tests (tests/enrichment_orchestration_tests.rs + an in-crate watch
unit test) each fail on the pre-fix code and pass after:
- enrich --kev fetches the mocked KEV catalog and the output SBOM carries the
  sbom-tools:kev property;
- query --offline makes ZERO network requests (the blocker; httpmock asserts 0
  hits);
- a config-file enrichment block (enable_kev) and offline:true take effect for
  query;
- enrich_sbom_full cannot re-enable a globally-set offline;
- enrich_watched_sbom runs HuggingFace and injects the weight hash.

fix(tui): correct view list-click hit-testing; gate un-verifiable tabs (#289)

Mouse list-clicks in the single-SBOM view used a fixed `list_start_row = 4`
as the origin, but content starts at row 5 and every tab's list body is
lower still (Tree/Dependencies at row 8, Licenses at row 10), so a click
selected the wrong row on every tab — and the arms ignored each list's
scroll offset entirely (only Source added it, and even that was
mis-origined).

Replace the fixed origin with `view_list_body_start(tab)`, which returns
each tab's real first-data row (derived from the layout + verified against
the view_* render snapshots) and adds the tab's persisted scroll offset,
clamped to the item count:
- Tree      -> tree_state.offset      (body_start 8)
- Licenses  -> license_state.scroll_offset (10)
- Dependencies -> dependency_state.scroll_offset (8)

Tabs whose list origin is runtime-variable (Source: breadcrumb row),
line-scrolled (Quality), or whose offset is not persisted render-exact
(Vulnerabilities/Compliance, crypto/AI list tabs) return None and are left
as no-ops — a no-op is strictly better than selecting the wrong row.
Un-gating those (and the diff-stack handler, whose fixtures don't populate
the lists and whose offsets aren't render-exact) is a tracked follow-up,
best done by recording the rendered list rect at draw time.

Test: renders each supported tab, finds a distinctive item's real row in
the buffer, clicks it, and asserts the selected index matches — so a wrong
body_start fails the test. No render change; snapshots unchanged.

fix(tui): unify multi-diff selection on one display-index space (#290)

The multi-comparison dashboard used `selected_target` inconsistently: the
Targets list highlighted by *display* index (position in the filtered +
sorted list), but the details side-panel and the detail modal looked it up
as a *raw* `result.comparisons` index — so under any sort or filter the
details showed a different comparison than the highlighted row. Search made
it worse: matches were raw indices, so both the match highlight and
jump-to-match landed on the wrong rows.

Introduce `ordered_comparison_indices(result, state)` — the raw indices in
display order (filter + sort + direction) — as the single source of truth,
and route the list, the details panel, the modal, and search through it:
- details panel / modal resolve `order[selected_target]` (out-of-range ->
  no comparison, safe under an active filter);
- search matches are stored as display indices, fixing both the match
  highlight and jump-to-match;
- toggling the filter resyncs the navigation bound (`total_targets`) to the
  visible count and clamps `selected_target`.

Also fix the Name-sort inversion: every key now uses a descending base order
so the shared Ascending reverse yields A→Z (Name previously used an
ascending base and inverted, showing Z→A on Ascending).

Adds `test_support::demo_multi_diff()` (a real `MultiDiffEngine` result over
two distinctly-named targets) and unit tests: Ascending Name is A→Z and
reorders the raw indices (so raw-index details would be wrong), Descending
is its reverse, and the vulnerabilities filter keeps only matching targets.
Rendering is otherwise unchanged (list rows build from the same ordering).

fix(tui): single-dispatch diff key handler (tab-first precedence) (#298)

The diff key dispatcher ran three matches unconditionally in series —
global bindings, then the active tab's handler, then the mode handler —
so every key bound by *both* the global layer and a tab/mode handler
fired twice. This is the confirmed collision set: `/` (global search +
SideBySide's own search), `p` (cycle-policy + panel focus), and `1`-`8`
(tab-select preempting Components' quick filters).

Restructure into a single dispatch with a `consumed` contract: the active
tab (`dispatch_tab_key`) and multi-comparison mode (`dispatch_mode_key`)
get first crack and now return whether they consumed the key; only keys
neither consumed reach the new `handle_global_fallback`. A tab-local
binding therefore wins over a colliding global one instead of both
firing.

All nine tab bridges and the three mode handlers now return `bool`
(derived from `EventResult != Ignored`, plus the data-dependent fallback).
The load-bearing guard: the four tabs whose global `select_*` is a no-op
(SideBySide/Quality/Compliance/GraphChanges) consume `j`/`k`/PageUp/Down
locally, so navigation is never starved; list tabs still defer nav to the
global handler. `Tab` is stripped from the Components/Licenses/SideBySide
views (panel focus stays on `p`/arrows) so it always reaches global
tab-switching, and `q` is consumed by no normal-mode tab, so quit and tab
cycling can never be shadowed — no reserved-key phase needed.

Adds `dispatch_precedence_tests`: per-tab assertions on the routing bool
(data-independent) covering nav layering, the three collisions resolving
tab-first, universal keys never being consumed, and end-to-end dispatch.

fix(matching): unify scoring behind one tier pipeline; kill wrong-neighbor and cross-ecosystem false merges

Four coupled matching-quality defects, fixed as one rewrite of
FuzzyMatcher around a single score_pair pipeline:

1. Score-tier inversion. Exact-name matches returned a flat 0.90 while
   near-miss fuzzy neighbors scored ~0.95+, so the (optimal) assignment
   systematically preferred wrong neighbors. Ground-truth A/B: the old
   scoring recovered only 4/100 identical-name version bumps; on
   convention-named fixtures it mispaired 100/100 and 999/1000. Name
   identity (ecosystem-normalized or case-insensitive raw) now anchors
   at 1.0 at tier level — before alias, fuzzy, AND multi-field scoring —
   and non-identical names cap at 0.99, so an exact-name counterpart
   strictly dominates in every scoring mode. New recovers 100% with no
   loss of legitimate fuzzy-rename recall (15/15, 150/150 in A/B).

2. Cross-ecosystem false merges. npm/redis vs pypi/redis merged at an
   unpenalized 1.0 via the index prefix fallback; the DB path admitted
   pairs at 0.80 below the user's threshold; the two engine paths
   implemented divergent policies. Policy now lives inside match_score:
   components from KNOWN-different ecosystems only match through the
   curated CrossEcosystemDb, with score_penalty and min_score applied
   uniformly regardless of which candidate source surfaced the pair.
   Unknown/Generic ecosystems don't engage the gate (a non-canonical
   purl spelling from another tool is missing information, not a
   substitution). Engine paths reduced to pure candidate generation.
   A/B: 7/7 seeded ecosystem substitutions previously merged silently;
   now all surface as added+removed. pypi/regex -> cargo/regex (curated)
   still matches, at 0.90 with tier CrossEcosystem.

3. Three divergent scoring formulas. match_components, match_detailed,
   and explain_match disagreed (a token-matched pair carried a "no
   match" explanation; match_detailed ignored field_weights). All three
   now read the same score_pair outcome and can no longer disagree;
   explanations show the full real formula (token/phonetic components,
   penalties, caps) and explain rejections ("different ecosystems with
   no curated equivalence").

4. Dead knobs and wrong aliases. use_aliases/use_ecosystem_rules now
   gate their tiers. The builtin alias table remains opt-in and drops
   entries that are related-but-distinct packages, not identity aliases
   (react/react-dom, webpack/webpack-cli, lodash/lodash-es and .merge/
   .get, attrs/attr, zipp/zipfile, opencv-python-headless, and the
   cross-ecosystem yaml/json families, whose job belongs to
   CrossEcosystemDb).

Downstream alignment: MatchTier::NameIdentity and ::CrossEcosystem
variants (non_exhaustive enum); exact-match metric boundary moved to
>= 0.995 so a capped 0.99 near-miss cannot count as exact;
PackageFamily::contains lowercases symmetrically with the DB index;
CrossEcosystemDb::equivalence() offers an allocation-light verified-
aware lookup. Behavior notes: cross-eco candidates are gated at the
fuzzy threshold like every other source, so min_score only bites above
it; identical-name multi-field pairs short-circuit to 1.0 (parity with
the old EcosystemRule-before-multi-field ordering).

noise), adversarial audit (two found defects fixed with regression
tests: fully-penalized pairs no longer "match at 0.0" when

mutation testing (all 5 mutations of the fixes are caught by the new
tests). Golden/TUI snapshot updates hand-reviewed: EcosystemRule
matches rescore 0.90 -> 1.0, richer fuzzy breakdowns, one Fuzzy ->

fix(diff): close every stale-splice and hash-blindness hole in incremental diffing

The incremental path (used by every diff-multi/timeline/matrix pairwise
diff) spliced sections from the previous pair's cached result whenever a
section hash looked clean — but the hashes missed real inputs, and the
content hashes underneath them missed real fields, so diffs served stale
or silently empty output. Verified end-to-end: seven reproduction
scenarios all broken at the previous commit and fixed here, including a
timeline run where 4 of 6 pairwise results were wrong as a CVE moved
between components across revisions.

Section hashes (incremental.rs) now carry an explicit contract — a hash
must cover every input its section computer reads — and cover edge
scope, license/vulnerability ownership (a CVE or license moving between
components was invisible), severity, CVSS, KEV/EPSS, and effective VEX.

diff_sections (engine.rs) is deduplicated with diff() into shared
compute_sections/finalize_result routines, so match metrics, the graph
diff, semantic score, and summary refresh on every partial hit (all
previously carried the prior pair's values) and the two paths cannot
drift again. Sections whose computers read the component MATCHES —
dependencies, licenses, vulnerabilities — rerun whenever components are
dirty (matches derive from component content; a rename spliced a stale
empty dependency diff), and vulnerabilities also rerun on edge changes
(VulnerabilityDetail.component_depth derives from the graph). Semantic
score now normalizes against the rule-filtered SBOMs on both paths.

Component::calculate_content_hash (sbom.rs) tags and length-prefixes
every field — raw concatenation let a dropped "MIT" license plus a
gained "MIT" supplier collide, and ml training-dataset/performance-
metric lists were byte-indistinguishable — and now covers vulnerability
severity/VEX/CVSS/source/CWEs/description/published/KEV dates,
ecosystem, group, crypto classical_security_level, and protocol
version, all previously hash-invisible (an SBOM pair differing only in
a CVSS score short-circuited as "identical").

Hash freshness at the sources: CycloneDX and SPDX3 recompute component
hashes after attaching vulnerabilities/VEX (both parsers hashed before
attachment, so vulnerability content was absent from every hash);
enrich_sbom_full and the vex CLI flow refresh hashes after enrichment
mutates vulnerability content.

Also: IncrementalDiffEngine bypasses the cache entirely for
content_hash==0 SBOMs (hand-built pairs all collided on the (0,0) key
and were served each other's results), and matched pairs differing only
in name/ecosystem now emit field changes instead of vanishing from the
modified section.

Verified by a 3-way workflow plus a delta re-audit: A/B reproductions
(7/7 scenarios OLD-broken/NEW-correct, timeline divergence eliminated,
4k diff +1.9%, richer hashing +0.4ms per incremental diff), a
field-coverage map proving every serialized VulnerabilityDetail field
is now covered, 8/8 mutations killed, and 12 new regression tests each

  them ("dependsOn" → "DEPENDSON"), which matched no arm, so every such
  relationship fell to the catch-all and produced a mis-typed
  Other("dependsOn") edge — silent graph corruption not recognized as a
  dependency. A new normalize_relationship_type() maps both camelCase
  and underscore forms to a canonical UPPER_SNAKE key.
- Inverse relationships (*_DEPENDENCY_OF, *_TOOL_OF, GENERATED_FROM)
  were emitted in the same from→to direction as their forward
  counterparts — a backwards graph (the SPDX 2 parser already swaps
  these). add_dependency_edge now takes a swap flag; "A dependencyOf B"
  correctly yields B→A. GENERATED_FROM swaps, GENERATES does not;
  CONTAINS/ANCESTOR_OF/PATCH_APPLIED keep their natural direction.

SPDX 3.0 @graph envelope:
- The canonical flat-graph serialization ({"@graph":[…]}, emitted by
  pyspdx and the spec examples) parsed to a silently empty SBOM — only
  the inline `element` array was read. The parser now chains `@graph`
  into the element pipeline, and lifts document metadata (name,
  creationInfo, rootElement → primary component) from the in-graph
  SpdxDocument node so CRA compliance still sees the primary component.

SPDX tag-value:
- Multi-line <text>…</text> free-form fields are accumulated as one
  value; previously each inner line was reparsed as a top-level tag,
  letting a crafted description inject SPDXID/Created. Verified: an
  injected "SPDXID: SPDXRef-EVIL" inside a copyright <text> block no
  longer takes effect.
- A File section (FileName) now closes the current package, so a File's
  SPDXID can't clobber the package's canonical id (tag-value packages
  have no explicit terminator). First inline tests for the SPDX 2 parser.

Verified by workflow: spec-conformance A/B vs main (every camelCase /
inverse / @graph / tag-value case fixed with correct edge directions;
all fixtures parse identically or with corrections, no regression) and
an adversarial audit (no correctness defect; its flagged @graph-metadata
gap is closed here). 13 new parser tests; full suite green, clippy
-D warnings and fmt clean.

fix(parsers): strip UTF-8 BOM, restore streaming metadata, harden format detection against misrouting

Third cluster from the parsers audit — detection and streaming. All
three fixes verified by A/B against the previous commit plus an
adversarial audit; zero regressions across the 23-fixture corpus and
1108 lib tests.

UTF-8 BOM:
- str::trim() does not strip U+FEFF, so a BOM-prefixed but otherwise
  valid SBOM failed detection and parsing on every path (JSON, XML,
  tag-value, and the reader/streaming path). A shared strip_bom() is
  now applied at every parser's detect()/parse_str(), and
  FormatDetector::parse_reader physically consumes the BOM bytes from
  the underlying reader (via BufRead::consume) before the reader-based
  parse, since serde_json::from_reader can't be fixed with a
  string-level strip.

Streaming metadata loss:
- ParseEvent::Metadata carried only DocumentMetadata; primary_component_id
  and extensions live on NormalizedSbom, not DocumentMetadata, and had no
  event to travel through. StreamingIterator::collect_sbom — the
  library's own advertised way to reconstruct a full NormalizedSbom from
  the event stream — always produced primary_component_id=None and
  default extensions regardless of what the source document declared.
  Metadata now carries a boxed ParsedMetadata { document,
  primary_component_id, extensions } (boxed per clippy::large_enum_variant,
  matching the existing Component(Box<_>) pattern), and collect_sbom
  restores both onto the reconstructed sbom.

Detection misrouting — the deepest fix in this cluster:
- Marker checks (bomFormat, specVersion, spdxVersion, SPDXID, @context,
  etc.) scanned the whole raw document as a substring, so a component or
  property VALUE that happened to equal a marker word (e.g. a component
  literally named "spdxVersion") could trip an unrelated format's
  detection. contains_json_key() now requires the marker to appear as an
  actual JSON key (quote+word+quote+colon), not a coincidental value.
- The SPDX 3.0 short-circuit (return immediately on HIGH confidence,
  before CycloneDX/SPDX were even computed) let a document satisfying
  SPDX3's substring quirks (@context + "spdx3" anywhere) silently
  misroute a valid CycloneDX document to the SPDX3 parser, which
  returned Ok with an EMPTY SBOM rather than an error. All three
  detectors are now computed before any selection
  (select_best_of_three), and a genuine tie at the top confidence is
  reported as ambiguous rather than resolved by an arbitrary priority
  order — this is what closes both the misroute-then-reject and the
  misroute-to-silently-empty bugs at the root, not just their specific
  reproductions. The bare "spdx3" substring fallback (no namespace URL)
  was dropped; verified against the real SPDX 3.0.1 spec that the
  surviving spdx.org/rdf/3 URL check covers every real-world document.

15 new tests (BOM on all three parsers/reader path, key-vs-value
detection, tie-as-ambiguous, streaming metadata round-trip including
the absent-primary-component case). Full suite green, clippy
-D warnings and fmt clean, no snapshot churn.

Documented, deliberate trade-off (noted by the audit, not fixed): the
non-streaming full-content detection path no longer short-circuits away
from computing all three detectors for a large SPDX 3.0 document, a
narrow scanning-cost increase scoped to that one case — reintroducing
the short-circuit would reintroduce the misrouting bug it exists to fix.

fix(parsers): make content hashing deterministic + close SPDX3/VEX fuzz and reader-path coverage gaps

Final cluster from the parsers audit — the "coverage" cluster, which
turned out to contain two real defects behind the missing tests.

Content-hash determinism (the defect):
- All three parsers substituted Utc::now() when a document had no (or an
  unparseable) creation timestamp, and DocumentMetadata.created is folded
  into NormalizedSbom's content hash — so a timestamp-less SBOM hashed
  DIFFERENTLY on every parse, silently defeating the diff engine's
  identity check and the incremental cache key. The fallback is now
  DateTime::UNIX_EPOCH, an honest deterministic "unknown" sentinel.
  Verified: OLD hashes a timestamp-less doc differently across parses
  (even with a sleep between them); NEW is byte-identical, and
  timestamped documents hash identically OLD vs NEW (no change for docs
  that carry a timestamp). The one test that reparsed identical bytes
  asserted nothing ("hash might differ … but should be consistent"); it
  now asserts equality, plus a cross-format determinism test.

Epoch-sentinel handling (so the fix doesn't produce misleading output):
- New DocumentMetadata::has_known_timestamp() centralizes "real timestamp
  vs. the epoch sentinel". CRA Art. 13(3) now reports "no creation
  timestamp" instead of a false "SBOM is 20640 days old"; ProvenanceMetrics
  gains timestamp_known (serde-default true for back-compat), is_fresh is
  false for timestamp-less docs (the old fallback silently granted them
  freshness credit — the actual scoring bug), and the age reports 0 rather
  than ~20000; the TUI overview and quality panels show "unknown" instead
  of "56 years ago"/1970. The two BSI checks that already tested
  timestamp() <= 0 were dead code under the old Utc::now() fallback and now
  correctly fire; their stale "default is Utc::now()" comments are updated.

RDF/XML streaming (defect found by the new reader-equivalence test):
- FormatDetector::parse_reader matched the SPDX variant "RDF" but detect()
  reports "RDF/XML", so every RDF/XML document sent through the
  reader/streaming path was misrouted to the JSON reader and failed. Fixed.

Fuzz + reader coverage:
- New fuzz_spdx3_json target (the 1984-line, loosest-deserializing parser
  had none), exercising both the inline-element and canonical @graph
  envelopes; wired into the CI fuzz matrix. The CycloneDX fuzzer now also
  wraps input as a vulnerability so apply_vulnerability — the most
  security-sensitive conversion path — is reachable (it never was). Four
  seed corpus files added (SPDX3 element/graph, the security-profile
  fixture, a CycloneDX doc with ratings/analysis/affects).
- Reader-vs-string equivalence tests across all format variants (the
  serde_json::from_reader path was near-untested and diverged, per above).

Verified by workflow: determinism A/B (all four timestamp-less formats
nondeterministic on OLD, identical on NEW; timestamped unchanged; all 42
parseable fixtures hash-stable), fuzz smoke (crate builds, seeds reach
apply_vulnerability and the spdx3 graph path, CI matrix updated), and a
blast-radius audit of every DocumentMetadata.created consumer (the audit
caught one missed TUI overview site, fixed here). Full suite green
(1644 tests), clippy -D warnings and fmt clean, no snapshot churn.

Merge pull request #300 from sbom-tool/audit/parsers

fix(enrichment): correct VEX status mapping and stop external VEX from silently suppressing real vulnerabilities

First cluster from the enrichment security audit — the VEX overlay path,
where a bug silently misreports a real vulnerability. All four defects
converge on that failure mode and are verified end-to-end through
VexEnricher::from_files().enrich_sbom() against the previous commit.

CSAF status-mapping inversions (csaf.rs):
- product_status.last_affected mapped to VexState::Fixed, but CSAF 2.0
  §3.2.3.4 defines it as the LAST versions KNOWN AFFECTED — those versions
  ARE vulnerable. Fixed is non-actionable, so a genuinely-affected
  component was silently suppressed. Now maps to Affected.
- product_status.recommended mapped to Affected, but it is the
  vendor-recommended FIXED version — a safe component was flagged as
  affected (false positive). Now maps to Fixed.
- Added the missing first_affected field (→ Affected); documented the full
  8-member product_status mapping inline.

CSAF global-suppression (csaf.rs + mod.rs):
- A product_status entry whose product_id did not resolve to a PURL was
  promoted to the global vuln-only table, which applies to EVERY component
  carrying that CVE. A CPE-only or unresolvable product under
  known_not_affected thus suppressed the CVE across unrelated components.
  A/B: OLD applied NotAffected to both of two unrelated components; NEW to
  neither. Unresolvable products are now dropped (counted + warned),
  matching the OpenVEX path, which already skipped them with a comment
  explaining exactly this risk — the two paths had been contradicting
  each other. CSAF has no document-wide statement, so nothing legitimate
  is dropped.

CycloneDX VEX (cyclonedx_vex.rs + mod.rs):
- Component-scoped statements are keyed by affects[].ref (a bom-ref, which
  lands in the component's format_id), but enrich_sbom looked them up only
  by PURL — so opaque-bom-ref statements silently never applied. The
  lookup now tries (vuln, purl) then (vuln, format_id). Empty bom-refs are
  rejected at the producer.
- analysis.state "exploitable" collapsed to UnderInvestigation; it is a
  live actionable threat. Now maps to Affected (with resolved_with_pedigree
  → Fixed), byte-identical to the SBOM parser's impactAnalysisState mapping.

Verified: end-to-end suppression A/B (6/6 cases fixed, no regression on
correctly-resolved CSAF or the OpenVEX path) and a CSAF-2.0/CycloneDX
spec-conformance audit (all 8 product_status members spec-correct, CDX
mapping matches the parser). 5 new/updated tests; full suite green
(1646 tests), clippy -D warnings and fmt clean, no snapshot churn.

fix(enrichment): validate OSV result attribution and bound hydration fan-out

Second cluster from the enrichment security audit — OSV attachment
integrity. The same false-negative failure mode as the VEX cluster: a
component silently gets the wrong vulnerabilities, or none.

Positional-zip misattribution (client.rs + mod.rs):
- enrich() attached querybatch results to components by array POSITION
  (to_fetch.zip(flatten(results))) with no count or identity check — the
  sole determinant of vuln→component attachment, and there is no local
  version matching to catch a mistake. A truncated response silently
  under-enriched (dropped a component's vulns); an extra/shifted response
  attached a vulnerability to the WRONG component with no error, and the
  wrong result was cached for the TTL. The OSV querybatch contract is
  exactly one result per query, in order, and pagination never changes
  result cardinality — so query_batch now validates results.len() ==
  chunk.len() per chunk and rejects a violation as InvalidResponse
  (fail-safe: no enrichment beats wrong enrichment). enrich() keeps a
  defensive total-count guard that skips all attachment on any mismatch
  and records an error rather than guessing by position.
  A/B: OLD attached a vuln to a SAFE component with no error signal; NEW
  refuses and records the contract violation.

Hydration fan-out cap (mod.rs):
- hydrate_vulns issued one sequential /v1/vulns/{id} GET per vuln stub,
  and the stub count is supplied by the (untrusted) querybatch response —
  unbounded request amplification. A per-run MAX_HYDRATION_REQUESTS
  budget (10_000, shared across all components) now bounds it; on
  exhaustion the remaining advisories fall back to id-only stubs and the
  result is marked incomplete so it is not cached as authoritative. A
  dedicated budget_hit flag drives the warning so it never false-fires on
  exactly-N legitimate hydrations.

Negative-cache correctness (verified, no behavior change):
- The existing `complete` flag already gates caching correctly — a
  genuine empty result (no vulns) is cached (correct negative caching)
  while a failed hydration (404/5xx) is not cached and is retried.
  Fixing the positional zip closed the remaining "wrong/empty result
  cached for the wrong component" vector. Added tests pinning both.

Verified: misattribution A/B via httpmock (truncation + extra-result
classes both fail-safe in NEW, were misattributing/suppressing in OLD;
well-formed control unchanged; genuine empties cached, failures retried)
and an adversarial audit confirming the count check matches the real OSV
querybatch API contract. 3 new tests; full suite green, clippy
-D warnings and fmt clean.

Known follow-up (pre-existing, out of scope): OSV next_page_token
pagination is not followed, so a component with >1000 advisories
truncates to page 1 (does not affect the result-count contract).
