fix(enrichment): bound every untrusted response read and the EPSS gzip decompression

Third cluster from the enrichment security audit — DoS hardening. Closes
the OOM/hang vectors reachable from a hostile, MITM'd, or
config-overridden endpoint (or a compromised registry mirror). Audit
confirms no unbounded untrusted-body read remains in src/enrichment.

Bounded response reads (route through source::read_bounded, the 256 MiB
cap KEV/EPSS/HuggingFace already used):
- OSV was the one client that skipped it: the querybatch body, the
  get_vulnerability body, and the error body (previously an unbounded
  response.text()) now read_bounded + serde_json::from_slice
  (osv/client.rs).
- Dependency-staleness registry queries — npm/PyPI/crates.io — parsed
  the full response into serde_json::Value unbounded (registry.rs); now
  bounded.
- endoflife.date product-list and cycles reads (eol/client.rs); now
  bounded.

EPSS decompression bomb:
- decode_maybe_gzip capped the COMPRESSED body (256 MiB) but then
  GzDecoder::read_to_string with no output cap — gzip expands up to
  ~1000:1, so a compliant compressed body could decompress into a
  ~250 GiB allocation (OOM). It now reads through Take(max+1) and
  rejects an overrun, bounding the DECOMPRESSED allocation. Split out
  decode_maybe_gzip_with_max (mirroring source::read_bounded_with_max)
  so the bomb rejection is testable with a small payload: the new test
  gzips 1 MiB of zeros (~1000:1) and confirms rejection under a small
  cap and clean decode under a large one.

OSV retry backoff:
- The retry delay was `Duration::from_secs(1 << (attempt - 1))` — an
  unchecked shift that overflows (uncapped multi-year sleep, and a debug
  panic at large attempt counts) for a big configured max_retries. Now
  uses the shared checked+capped backoff_delay (checked_shl + MAX_BACKOFF).

read_bounded (oversized rejection) and backoff_delay (cap/overflow) are
already unit-tested in source.rs, so these are wiring changes to proven
helpers; the existing OSV/EOL/registry/EPSS http tests confirm the happy
paths are unchanged.

Verified: DoS-bound A/B (gzip bomb rejected + legit gzip still loads; all
four unbounded-read families now bounded; backoff capped) and an
adversarial audit confirming no unbounded untrusted-body read remains.
1 new test; full suite green (1650 tests), clippy -D warnings and fmt
clean, no snapshot churn.

fix(enrichment): harden the network trust surface (URL validation, hash provenance, cache integrity)

Final cluster from the enrichment security audit — the network trust
surface. Untrusted config, untrusted SBOM-derived request paths, and
untrusted network/cache data crossing into trusted outputs.

Config-URL validation (config/validation.rs):
- api_base/kev_url/epss_url/huggingface_url overrides were unvalidated,
  accepting non-http schemes (file://, …) and malformed URLs for
  endpoints that supply security data. validate() now requires each to be
  a well-formed http(s) URL with a host. Private/self-hosted hosts stay
  allowed (legitimate internal mirrors); the check is dependency-light so
  it runs without the enrichment feature.

HuggingFace hash provenance — stop network hashes becoming the verify
baseline (model/metadata.rs, verification/model_dir.rs, huggingface):
- `verify --model-dir` treated ALL component.hashes as the trusted
  integrity baseline, and the HF enricher injected registry/cache-sourced
  sha256 hashes into that list — so the tool verified a local file
  against a hash it fetched from the same place (circular trust; a
  poisoned cache or overridden URL sets the hash it is checked against).
  Hash gains a HashProvenance marker (Authored vs Enriched); PartialEq/
  Eq/Hash IGNORE it and it is #[serde(skip)], so dedup, content-hashing,
  and SBOM emission are byte-identical (verified: content_hash and
  CycloneDX/SPDX emit unchanged). verify now trusts only Authored hashes;
  enriched hashes still satisfy AI-010.

HuggingFace model_id injection (huggingface/client.rs):
- model_id (from untrusted SBOM PURL/URL fields) was interpolated
  unencoded into the request URL and the cache filename. resolve() — the
  single choke point for both — now validates it against HuggingFace's
  repo-id grammar and skips anything malformed (../ , extra /, ?, #, …).

Cache-filename collisions (huggingface, staleness/registry, eol):
- The per-source cache_filename did replace(['/',':'],"_"), which is
  non-injective: npm:x / npm/x / npm_x — and EleutherAI/gpt-neo vs
  EleutherAI_gpt-neo — collapsed to one file, mis-attributing one entry's
  data to another. All three now hash the key (source::key_to_filename,
  SHA256 hex): collision-free and traversal-safe.

Offline staleness bound (source.rs):
- Offline mode served arbitrarily-expired cache entries (stale-if-offline)
  with only a log line — presenting months-old vuln data as current. It
  now bounds offline staleness at 90 days past TTL: air-gapped runs still
  work, but data too old to trust is a hard miss.

Verified: trust-boundary A/B (verify no longer trusts enriched hashes —
was circular; content-hash + CycloneDX/SPDX emit byte-identical; URL/
model_id/collision/staleness all fixed) and an adversarial audit (which
caught the HF cache still colliding for distinct valid ids — fixed here
and pinned by a test). 7 new tests; full suite green (1656 tests),
clippy -D warnings and fmt clean, no snapshot churn.

fix(quality): stop crypto-compliance false-passes (vacuous CNSA2/PQC, classical crypto, undocumented CBOM)

First cluster from the quality/compliance audit — the flagship problem: a
tool advertising CNSA 2.0 / NIST PQC checking green-lit SBOMs it should
reject, so a user could certify quantum-safety the tool never actually
verified. The audit's threat model is a false regulatory claim; every fix
here flips a false verdict in the correct direction, and the A/B confirms
no over-correction (legitimate PQC crypto still passes).

Vacuous pass on empty inventory:
- check_cnsa2 / check_nist_pqc iterated components, `continue`d past every
  non-Cryptographic one, and emitted nothing — so a plain application SBOM
  (no CBOM) reported COMPLIANT for CNSA 2.0 and NIST PQC. They now emit an
  Error (SBOM-CNSA2-000 / SBOM-PQC-000) when zero cryptographic assets were
  evaluated: a PQC-readiness verdict must not be "compliant" having checked
  nothing.

Classical quantum-vulnerable crypto passed PQC:
- PQC-001 fired only when nistQuantumSecurityLevel == Some(0), and the
  broken-family list had no classical asymmetric algorithm — so an RSA /
  ECDSA / ECDH / DH / DSA CBOM with an unset quantum level (the common
  real-world case) passed NIST PQC. A new
  AlgorithmProperties::is_classical_quantum_vulnerable() flags these on the
  family alone (broken by Shor's algorithm regardless of key size); PQC-001
  now fires on it, and the quantum_vulnerable_count metric counts it.

Grade-A for undocumented crypto:
- CryptographyMetrics incremented total_crypto_components BEFORE the
  crypto_properties guard, so a Cryptographic component with no
  cryptoProperties made has_data() true and the six CBOM sub-scores
  returned 100 on empty denominators (grade-A crypto for nothing
  documented). It now counts only documented assets, so the crypto score is
  N/A rather than 100.

CNSA gate escapes + ECC false-fail:
- The hash gate only matched family literally "SHA-2"/"SHA2" with param
  "256", so SHA-224 and family-form "SHA-256" escaped; it now catches both
  encodings. AES now requires an explicit 256 (via param or classical
  security level) instead of passing on an absent parameter.
- Conversely, the key-size check false-FAILED every ECC key (flat <2048),
  but an ECC key size is the curve bit-length (P-256 → 256 ≈ 128-bit
  security). Strong ECC curve sizes (255/256/384/448/521) are now adequate
  while RSA/finite-field still needs ≥2048; 512 is deliberately excluded so
  a factorable 512-bit RSA/DSA key is not passed as "strong ECC".

Verified: false-pass/false-fail A/B vs main (all four false-passes flip to
fail; ML-KEM-1024/ML-DSA-87/SHA-384/AES-256 clean CBOM stays compliant;
ECC P-256/P-384 no longer false-failed; RSA-1024 still flagged) and an
over-correction audit (no PQC family or hybrid trips the classical list;
it caught the 512-bit-RSA hole in the ECC allowlist, fixed here). 7 new
tests; two compliance TUI snapshots correctly flip a crypto-less fixture
from pass to fail. Full suite green (1649 tests), clippy -D warnings and
fmt clean.

fix(quality): make required compliance elements gate + reconcile quality exit code

Second cluster from the quality/compliance audit — gate mis-mappings where a
required element was declared mandatory but never actually failed the verdict,
plus a score/verdict exit-code inconsistency. Threat model is the same false
regulatory claim; each fix flips a false verdict in the correct direction, and
the A/B confirms a fully-complete SBOM is not newly false-failed.

Required elements now gate:
- NTIA "Timestamp" (one of the seven required minimum data fields) was a literal
  no-op: the check was skipped on the assumption "we always set a timestamp."
  But a missing/invalid source timestamp is stored as the UNIX_EPOCH sentinel,
  so it now gates on has_known_timestamp() with an Error (SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP)
  for NtiaMinimum/Comprehensive.
- EO 14028 §4(e) Supplier Name — a required NTIA element — was a non-gating
  Warning behind a >30% missing threshold while version and unique-id were
  Errors. It is now a gating Error on any missing supplier, consistent with the
  other required elements.
- BSI TR-03183-2 §5.3 mandatory component name was a comment-only no-op that
  claimed the name was "already enforced globally" — but the dedicated BSI
  checker never runs the generic component check, so a nameless component
  passed. It now enforces the name (SBOM-BSI-TR-03183-2-5-3).

False-fail fixed:
- CRA Art. 24 OSS-steward vulnerability-handling gate only inspected component
  external refs and the sidecar, ignoring the document-level
  vulnerability_disclosure_url / security_contact that its own doc comment says
  satisfy it. Those document fields now count (a strict OR-widening).

Score/verdict exit code:
- `quality` printed the compliance verdict ("NON-COMPLIANT (N errors)") but its
  only exit gate was --min-score, so a grade-A but non-compliant SBOM exited 0.
  Added an opt-in --fail-on-noncompliant flag that exits COMPLIANCE_ERRORS when
  the verdict is non-compliant; the default stays score-only so existing scripts

N/A stays compliant (deliberate): a standard that does not apply to an SBOM
(e.g. EU AI Act on a non-AI SBOM) is not a violation, so is_compliant is left
true — unlike the crypto case, where no crypto inventory under a *crypto*
standard means readiness cannot be asserted. The CRA "Default product class
under-gates" behavior is the intended CRA-P3.2 severity-tiering-by-class, not a
bug, and is left as-is.

Also aligned two registry default_severity entries (EO14028-SUPPLIER,
BSI-5-3) to the Error severity actually emitted, and expanded the Art.24
remediation message to mention the document-level satisfiers.

Verified: verdict A/B vs the crypto-cluster commit (all four gates flip in the
correct direction with the expected rule_ids; a fully-complete SBOM stays
compliant under NTIA/EO/BSI; the flag gates only when set, confirmed through the
built binary) and an over-correction audit (the widenings cannot introduce a
false-fail; compliant golden fixtures still pass zero errors). 4 new tests; full
suite green (1653 tests), clippy -D warnings and fmt clean; no golden/snapshot

fix(quality): count license/identifier metrics per-component, not per-entry

Third cluster from the quality audit — metric-counting bugs that inflated
scores by conflating per-entry counts with per-component denominators, plus
a fake SPDX validator. All fixes are in how metrics COUNT; the A/B confirms
a well-formed SBOM scores byte-identically before and after.

NOASSERTION counted as licensed:
- CompletenessMetrics and LicenseMetrics counted any non-empty declared list
  as "has license", but the CycloneDX parser emits declared=["NOASSERTION"]
  for empty license objects — so an SBOM with no real license data reported
  100% licensed. A component now needs at least one non-NOASSERTION entry
  (SPDX NONE still counts as documented: asserting no license exists is
  information; making no assertion is not). A/B: 4-of-5 NOASSERTION SBOM
  drops from 100% to 20% licensed.

SPDX validity was a substring check:
- is_valid_spdx_license accepted any string containing " OR "/" AND "/
  " WITH " — "GARBAGE OR NONSENSE" validated. Deleted; metrics now use the
  is_valid_spdx the model already computes in LicenseExpression::new via the
  spdx crate (LAX parse). Net direction is MORE accepting of real-world
  forms (GPL-2.0+, Zlib, MIT/Apache-2.0, case variants now valid; the old
  25-id list rejected them) while garbage operands finally fail.
- validate_spdx's NOASSERTION/NONE guard now matches whole tokens, so
  LicenseRef-NONEXCLUSIVE is no longer substring-rejected; and from_spdx_id
  validates instead of hardcoding is_valid_spdx=true now that scoring

fix(quality): make scoring monotonic and deterministic (vuln baseline, freshness, coverage clamp)

Fourth and final cluster from the quality audit — score-math defects where
the arithmetic itself produced perverse or unstable results.

Disclosing a vulnerability lowered the score:
- A bare VulnerabilityRef (no CVSS/CWE/remediation) scored the VulnDocs
  category 0, while an SBOM with NO vulnerability data got N/A and its
  weight redistributed — so disclosing was worse than stripping the data,
  punishing exactly the transparency an SBOM exists to provide.
  documentation_score now grants a 40-point disclosure baseline plus up to
  60 for quality (CVSS 24 / CWE 18 / remediation 18 — the old 40:30:30
  proportions preserved; fully documented still lands exactly on 100).
  A/B: the perverse gap halves (6.74 → 3.27 pts on the probe SBOM); the
  quality gradient survives (bare 40 < partial < full 100). The residual
  gap is deliberate: full parity would require rewarding disclosure above
  the SBOM's own average.

Freshness made scores non-deterministic:
- is_fresh (created < 90 days, live wall clock) carried 12 points of the
  provenance checklist, so identical SBOM bytes scored differently across
  midnight, and a future-dated document always counted fresh. Freshness is
  now display-only metadata: the checklist item is removed (denominator
  105 → 93 for CycloneDX), making the quality score a pure function of the
  document — the same determinism contract as the parser content-hash
  work. Future-dated documents no longer read as fresh. NOTE: fresh
  documents lose a little provenance ((S+12)/105 → S/93), stale and
  timestamp-less ones gain — that redistribution is the point. The TUI
  score explanation no longer cites freshness, and the two quality
  snapshots move by exactly the renormalization (9→10 / 10%→11%).

Cyclic graphs absorbed their own penalty:
- Dependency coverage uses an N/(N-1) denominator, so a fully-cyclic graph
  reached ~125% raw coverage and swallowed the cycle penalty before the
  final clamp (ring graph scored a perfect 100). Coverage now clamps to
  100 before penalties: the same ring scores 95 with its cycle visible;
  acyclic graphs are bit-identical.

Wrong-field recommendation + hardcoded flag:
- The "Add VCS URLs" recommendation derived missing-VCS from HASH coverage:
  it stayed silent for SBOMs with no VCS refs (all hashed) and fired for
  fully-VCS'd SBOMs missing hashes. AuditabilityMetrics is now plumbed into
  generate_recommendations and the count uses components_with_vcs.
- CompletenessMetrics.has_timestamp was hardcoded true; it now reports
  has_known_timestamp() (score-neutral; TUI checklist and reports only).

the measured amounts; a well-formed SBOM's full report JSON differs in
exactly two fields — the provenance renormalization) and an adversarial

fix(parsers): parse canonical SPDX 3.0.1 JSON-LD documents (#305)

Canonical SPDX 3.0.1 @graph documents (the spec examples, tools-java,
pyspdx output) failed to parse:

- Element `creationInfo` is a blank-node string ref in canonical
  serializations ("creationInfo": "_:ci"); typing it as an inline
  struct hard-failed the whole document. Accept both schema-valid
  forms (the JSON schema's CreationInfo_derived is anyOf
  [object, ref]) via an untagged string-or-object representation.
- Standalone CreationInfo graph nodes fell into the Unknown catch-all,
  discarding created/createdBy/createdUsing/specVersion. Index them by
  "@id" and resolve the document's ref through them (with a
  single-node fallback when nothing references one resolvably).
- serde's internally-tagged enum consumes the `type` key, so
  Spdx3Agent's tag field was always None and every creator was
  classified as a Tool — has_org_creator could never pass for SPDX 3
  input. Resolve the agent kind from the matched enum variant instead.
- software_Sbom had no type mapping and collections were unhandled, so
  SpdxDocument.rootElement -> Sbom -> package never resolved a primary
  component (a 12-point provenance metric). Alias the tag and follow
  one bounded level of collection rootElement indirection.
- Canonical profile-prefixed property names (software_*,
  simplelicensing_*, security_* payloads) were ignored as unknown
  fields: packages parsed without versions, security assessments
  without CVSS scores or VEX justifications. Add serde aliases;
  software_byteRange/lineRange accept the canonical
  PositiveIntegerRange object form via a lenient deserializer that
  never fails the document.

v0.1.22 additionally lacked @graph handling entirely (the key was
silently ignored -> "Parsed 0 components", 0.9/100 quality score);
that half was fixed by 0bb3971, and this completes canonical-document
support. The issue reproducer is checked in verbatim as a regression
test alongside nine more covering both creationInfo forms, agent-kind
resolution, prefixed properties, range objects, and the
Bom/Bundle/software_Sbom primary-component chain.

fix(parsers): CycloneDX correctness criticals — hard-fails, assemblies, services, VEX versions

A spec-conformance audit against the official bom-1.4..1.7 schemas found
five classes of critical defect in the CycloneDX parser; this fixes all
of them, in both the JSON and XML variants:

- Wrongly-required fields hard-failed spec-valid documents: supplier.name,
  property.value/name, vulnerability.id, and vulnerability.source.name are
  all optional per the schemas (organizationalEntity, vulnerability, and
  vulnerabilitySource have NO required properties; property requires name
  only in 1.6+ and nothing in 1.4/1.5). One name-less supplier anywhere
  aborted the entire parse. All are Option now, with explicit fallbacks:
  supplier name falls back to its URL; a vulnerability id falls back to
  its first reference id (carrying THAT reference's source), else an
  index-disambiguated UNKNOWN-{n} so distinct anonymous records cannot
  merge in id-keyed consumers.

- Nested component assemblies (component.components, recursive since 1.0)
  were silently dropped — undercounting inventory and discarding the
  dependencies and vulnerabilities that referenced nested bom-refs. They
  now parse via an iterative worklist (bounded by element count, no
  recursion), join the id_map, and preserve the hierarchy as Contains
  edges. metadata.component children included.

- Top-level services (SaaSBOM, 1.4+) were dropped entirely — SaaSBOMs
  parsed to empty. Services (and nested services) now convert to
  components typed Other("service"), with provider→supplier, declared
  licenses, endpoints/external references, and id_map registration.

- affects[].versions ignored per-entry status and dropped range entries:
  versions explicitly marked "unaffected" were reported as affected. Only
  entries with status "affected" (or absent — the spec default) are
  reported now, and vers range strings are kept.

- Hardening: the recursive XML models are only reachable behind an
  iterative depth pre-scan (MAX_XML_DEPTH=128, matching serde_json's
  effective cap on the JSON path) — without it, a crafted deeply-nested
  XML document would abort the process by stack overflow, since quick-xml
  enforces no recursion limit.

Verified against the official CycloneDX spec test documents (component
counts, tools forms, VEX detail unchanged) plus 9 new regression tests
covering every fix, including XML twins and the depth bomb.

fix(parsers): SPDX 2.x core data-loss gaps — documentDescribes, files, LicenseRef, CPE, purpose, emails

A spec-conformance audit against the SPDX 2.2/2.3 spec and official
examples found the SPDX 2.x parser silently dropping or misfiling
commonly-present data:

- documentDescribes was not modeled at all, so the 2.2-era primary-
  component mechanism never resolved (the tool's own remediation text
  told users to set exactly that field). Primary selection now unions
  documentDescribes with DESCRIBES/DESCRIBED_BY relationships and
  prefers a package over a file across both mechanisms.
- Top-level files and snippets were dropped entirely; relationships
  targeting them silently vanished. They now become ComponentType::File
  components (JSON + tag-value FileName blocks; matching the SPDX 3.0
  parser), joined by package.hasFiles containment edges (deduped
  against explicit CONTAINS relationships). Quality/compliance treat
  file entries as name+hash records: they are excluded from package
  completeness percentages and from version/supplier/identifier
  compliance requirements, so a file-cataloguing SBOM no longer emits
  thousands of spurious errors.
- hasExtractedLicensingInfos was never parsed: a bare LicenseRef-*
  declared/concluded expression now carries its resolved display name
  (new LicenseExpression.resolved_name, excluded from equality/
  hashing so license identity semantics are unchanged); tag-value
  LicenseID/LicenseName/ExtractedText blocks parse too.
- SECURITY external refs ignored referenceType: cpe22Type/cpe23Type now
  populate identifiers.cpe and swid populates identifiers.swid, while
  only advisory/fix/url remain advisory links — a CPE string can no
  longer masquerade as the document's vulnerability-disclosure URL
  (which false-passed EO 14028/CRA disclosure checks).
- primaryPackagePurpose (SPDX 2.3) now maps to ComponentType instead
  of every package being typed Library.
- Creator strings follow the §6.8 grammar: "(email)" is split into
  Creator.email (has_contact_email was structurally false for SPDX);
  supplier emails become an Organization contact; originator maps to
  Component.author (was a dead field).
- homepage → Website ref; downloadLocation → SourceDistribution ref,
  with the SPDX emitter preferring distribution refs when
  reconstructing downloadLocation so the field round-trips instead of
  being displaced by the homepage; summary is the description
  fallback; builtDate/releaseDate/validUntilDate parse, with the
  primary package's validUntilDate feeding support_end_date.
- Inverse relationships CONTAINED_BY/GENERATED_FROM/DESCENDANT_OF/
  EXPANDED_FROM_ARCHIVE now map (edges no longer depend on which
  spelling a generator picked); DOCUMENTATION_OF direction corrected.
- BLAKE3 checksums map to the typed variant; the has_tool_version
  metric recognizes the SPDX-mandated "toolname-version" form.
- New files/snippets/extracted-license entries deserialize leniently:
  one malformed entry is skipped, never failing the whole document.

On the official SPDXJSONExample: components 4 → 9 (packages + files +
snippet), dependency edges 1 → 4, CPE extracted, has_tool_version and
has_primary_component true, completeness percentages computed over
packages only.

fix(compliance): make CNSA2/PQC classification input-robust (allowlist semantics, OID/name fallback, protocol assets)

The CNSA 2.0 / NIST PQC checkers keyed every decision off the CycloneDX
1.7-only algorithmFamily string, so real-world 1.6 CBOMs (name/OID/
parameter only) passed both standards with zero violations, and CNSA 2.0
was a small blocklist instead of the exclusive allowlist the standard
defines. Defect classes fixed:

- One canonical classifier (model::classify_algorithm): normalizes
  family strings (case/separators, SHA1->SHA-1, TDES/DES-EDE3->3DES,
  ARC4->RC4), maps round-3 PQC names (Kyber->ML-KEM, Dilithium-2/3/5->
  ML-DSA-44/65/87, SPHINCS+->SLH-DSA, Falcon->FN-DSA), extracts trailing
  sizes (ML-KEM-768, AES-128), reads the OID (RSA/DSA/DH/EC arcs, SHA-1,
  MD5, SHA-2/3, AES key size from the OID arc, ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA,
  Ed25519/X25519), honours the previously-unread ellipticCurve field,
  and falls back to word-boundary name-token matching only when family
  and OID are both absent.
- check_cnsa2 rewritten as an allowlist: AES-256, SHA-384/512,
  ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, LMS/XMSS/HSS (SP 800-208). Broken algorithms
  (new SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005), recognized-but-not-CNSA algorithms (new
  SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-008: ChaCha20, Camellia, SHA-3, SLH-DSA, Falcon) and
  parameterless AES/ML-KEM/ML-DSA now Error; unclassifiable assets get a
  cannot-verify Warning (new SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN), never a pass. The
  duplicated CNSA2_VULNERABLE/BROKEN tables are deleted; Ed25519/Ed448/
  ECIES/ECMQV/ElGamal/DHE/ECDHE/EC no longer pass CNSA2.
- Protocol assets are evaluated under both standards: SSL or TLS!=1.3 is
  an Error under CNSA2 (SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-001), SSL or TLS<1.2 under PQC
  (SBOM-PQC-PROTO-001); cipher suites (resolved algorithm bom-refs plus
  word-boundary suite-name scan), IKEv2 transforms, and crypto refs are
  classified and flagged (SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-002 / SBOM-PQC-PROTO-002).
- CERT-001 resolves signatureAlgorithmRef through the bom-ref index to
  the referenced algorithm (opaque refs like "sig-algo-42" now checked),
  with token-match fallback on the raw ref; PQC gains the analogous
  SBOM-PQC-CERT-001.
- The CNSA2-000/PQC-000 inventory gates now count only assets that
  actually receive evaluation, so key material or unknown asset kinds
  can no longer satisfy the gate while receiving zero checks.

All new rule IDs are registered in the rule registry with CNSA2/NIST-PQC
standard refs and remediation. New CycloneDX 1.6 fixture (no
algorithmFamily) plus firing-and-silent tests for every changed rule; no
existing test expectations were changed.

fix(compliance): rebase BSI TR-03183-2 checker on v2.1.0 (format gate, SHA-512, ten required fields, tier corrections)

The BSI checker implemented a v2.0.0-era reading of TR-03183-2 with several
requirements mis-tiered against the current guideline. Rebase on v2.1.0
(2025-08-20, canonical: https://bsi.bund.de/dok/TR-03183-en):

- NEW §4 format gate (SBOM-BSI-TR-03183-2-4, Error): newly generated or
  updated SBOMs must be CycloneDX >= 1.6 or SPDX >= 3.0.1; versions are
  compared numerically (SPDX 3.0 < 3.0.1 fails), and the §7 transitional
  grace for v2.0.0 minimums ended 2026-02-20.
- Hash (§5.2.2): the normative clause names SHA-512, so the old "SHA-256 or
  stronger" acceptance was a false-pass — components whose hashes lack
  SHA-512 now Error (-5-4); components with no hash at all Warn (-5-4-MISSING)
  per the §3.2.1 legitimate-omission escape. Only author-attested hashes
  count (enriched hashes are not part of the document).
- Unique identifiers (purl/CPE) moved from gating Error to Warning
  (-5-2-4): §5.2.4 is the ADDITIONAL tier ("MUST additionally ... if it
  exists"), and existence is not machine-verifiable.
- REMOVED the tool-creator Error: v2.1.0 mandates no generation-tool field
  in any tier (Creator of the SBOM maps to Person/Organization, not
  metadata.tools).
- Document creator (§5.2.1): Error only when absent entirely (-5-1); a
  creator without a discernible email/URL is now a Warning (-5-1-CONTACT).
- NEW per-component required-field checks (§5.2.2): version Error
  (-VERSION), distribution licences Error (-LICENSE), component creator
  presence Warning (-CREATOR), dependency-enumeration completeness Warning
  (-5-5-COMPLETENESS, CycloneDX compositions).
- NEW §6.1 licence-naming Warning (-LICENSE-SPDX): licences must be named
  by SPDX identifier/expression; text is not a substitute.
- NEW §3.1 Warning (-3-1): an SBOM must not contain vulnerability
  information (Warning, not Error, because enrichment can attach findings
  to the same model field post-parse).
- Filename and executable/archive/structured properties are not modeled;
  documented as comment-only (no vacuous checks).
- Registry refs updated to v2.1.0 section numbers with per-rule
  remediations; SARIF hand-table entries added for every rule; canonical
  help URI switched to BSI's stable shortlink; docs/CRA_COMPLIANCE.md
  quick-mapping and reverse-map BSI columns rewritten for v2.1.0.
- Fixtures upgraded (SHA-512 hashes, author email, licences on primary,
  compositions) and tests added for every changed/new rule, including the
  deliberate expectation flips: SHA-256-only now fails, purl-less is
  Warning not Error, tool absence no longer errors, CycloneDX 1.5 / SPDX
  2.3 / SPDX 3.0 fail the gate while 1.6 / 3.0.1 pass.

fix(parsers): close SPDX3/CycloneDX gaps behind the BSI v2.1.0 gate (shared CreationInfo, software_ aliases, spec-version fabrication, completeness mapping, metadata.manufacturer, non-tool creator gate)

The new BSI TR-03183-2 v2.1.0 gate made SPDX >= 3.0.1 the only eligible
SPDX format and rebased the required-field checks, but parser-layer gaps
meant the gate's verdicts were wrong for exactly the documents it
mandates:

- SPDX3: canonical SPDX 3.0.1 JSON-LD (flat @graph with a shared
  {"type":"CreationInfo","@id":"_:creationinfo"} node referenced by
  string-valued creationInfo) hard-failed the parse with "invalid type:
  string", so no canonical SPDX document could obtain a BSI verdict at
  all. creationInfo now deserializes as an untagged object-or-reference
  enum; CreationInfo nodes are collected from the @graph by @id and the
  document's reference is resolved through them.

- SPDX3: the official 3.0.1 JSON-LD context prefixes software-profile
  properties (software_packageVersion, software_packageUrl, ...), but
  Spdx3Package/File/Snippet only accepted the unprefixed spellings while
  the ELEMENT types already aliased software_*. Conformant documents
  silently lost every version and purl, producing false BSI §5.2.2
  version Errors and §5.2.4 identifier Warnings. Both spellings now
  deserialize via serde aliases (byteRange/lineRange deliberately
  excluded: the canonical prefixed form is an object, and aliasing it
  onto a string field would turn an ignored key into a parse failure).
  Same treatment for the SimpleLicensing profile's property spellings,
  which feed the §5.2.2 licence Error.

- SPDX3: a document whose creationInfo carried no specVersion was
  assigned a fabricated "3.0", which the §4 gate then rejected as
  "SPDX 3.0 < 3.0.1" with a version the document never declared. The
  version now stays empty, and the checker's documented empty-skip
  applies. The EO 14028 / CRA machine-readable SPDX arms gain the same
  empty-skip so removing the fabricated value introduces no new false
  fires there (their CycloneDX arms already passed empty versions).

- SPDX3: Relationship.completeness was deserialized but never mapped,
  leaving completeness_declaration Unknown for every SPDX document and
  making the §5.2.2 completeness Warning unsatisfiable even for SPDX
  3.0.1 documents that declare it. Dependency relationships'
  completeness values now fold into CompletenessDeclaration (any
  incomplete > complete > noAssertion=NotSpecified > absent=Unknown);
  SPDX 2.x has no such field and correctly stays Unknown. The Warning
  message now names both mechanisms instead of only CycloneDX.

- SPDX3: Person/Organization agents resolved via createdBy were always
  typed Tool — serde's internally-tagged Spdx3Element enum consumes
  "type", so Spdx3Agent's own tag field never populated. The creator
  type is now resolved from the enum variant during the first pass
  (same pattern as resolved_vex_state). Latent before, load-bearing
  once the §5.2.1 gate distinguishes Tool from non-Tool creators.

- CycloneDX: BSI v2.1.0 Table 8 maps the required "Creator of the SBOM"
  to metadata.manufacturer, and the tool's own remediation text tells
  users to set it — but the parser never deserialized the field, so
  documents expressing their creator exactly as the TR prescribes were
  declared NON-COMPLIANT and following the remediation could not clear
  the finding. metadata.manufacturer (and the deprecated
  metadata.manufacture spelling) now parses into an Organization
  creator with its contact email; with no email, the first URL is
  folded into the name so the §5.2.1 email-or-URL fallback stays
  discernible.

- BSI §5.2.1: the creator Error gated on creators.is_empty(), so a
  tools-only SBOM (the default output of common generators) passed
  although the TR's own mapping explicitly excludes metadata.tools.
  The presence gate and the -CONTACT Warning now consider only non-Tool
  (Person/Organization) creators; tools-only is an Error. Deliberate
  expectation flip pinned by a new test.

- Added the missing regression test for the §5.2.2 SHA-512 rule's
  HashProvenance::Authored exclusion: an enriched SHA-512 alongside an
  authored SHA-256 still fires SBOM-BSI-TR-03183-2-5-4; enriched-only
  hashes count as hash-less (Warning), authored SHA-512 is silent.

Tests: firing + silent pairs per fix in the parser test modules and the
BSI checker tests; new canonical shared-creationinfo fixture under
tests/fixtures/spdx3/ with an end-to-end golden test asserting it
parses and clears the BSI gate with zero Errors. Full suite green
(49 suites), clippy --all-features clean vs base, cargo fmt applied.

fix(diff): non-TUI reports honour the CRA sidecar and product class like the TUI

The same `sbom-tools diff old.json new.json` invocation produced different
CRA verdicts depending on the output format: the TUI auto-discovered the
CRA sidecar next to the new SBOM and threaded it into its compliance
checkers, while the non-TUI report stage (and the per-reporter fallbacks in
the JSON/HTML/Markdown/SARIF generators) built bare
`ComplianceChecker::new(CraPhase2)` instances with no sidecar or product
class. A sidecar-supplied security contact, support end date, product
class, or high-risk-AI flag was silently ignored in `diff -o json|md|html|
sarif`.

Fix, with per-SBOM sidecar resolution as the documented design:

- pipeline/report_stage: pre-compute each side's CRA Phase 2 result with
  that SBOM's own auto-discovered sidecar (`<sbom>.cra.{json,yaml}`, stdin
  never resolves one) via a new shared `pipeline::discover_cra_sidecar()`.
  Each side of the diff is judged against the metadata shipped next to it,
  so a contact or product-class change between releases shows up in the
  diff instead of being masked by one side's evidence. `diff` has no
  `--cra-sidecar`/`--cra-product-class` flags, so auto-discovery is the
  only channel; the sidecar's own `productClass` is honoured by
  `ComplianceChecker::effective_product_class()` (same precedence as
  validate/view: sidecar wins).
- cli/diff (TUI path): switched from "new SBOM's sidecar applied to both
  sides" to the same per-SBOM resolution, so TUI and non-TUI reports agree
  by construction. `App::with_cra_sidecar` becomes
  `with_cra_sidecars(old, new)` and now also recomputes the summary-card
  CRA results, which `new_diff()` pre-computed bare — previously the TUI's
  own summary tab disagreed with its compliance tab.
- reporters: the duplicated `.unwrap_or_else(bare checker)` fallbacks in
  json/html/markdown/sarif (diff + view paths) are replaced by single
  `ReportConfig::{old,new,view}_cra_compliance_or_bare()` accessors; the
  bare computation survives only as a documented last resort for direct
  library callers, and every first-party pipeline now populates the
  pre-computed fields (report stage, view CLI, TUI diff export, ViewApp
  export) so exports match what is on screen.
- cli/view: audited — its non-TUI path already resolved the sidecar and
  product class correctly; unchanged.

New integration test drives the built binary end to end: `diff -o json`
with a sidecar adjacent to only one side must downgrade that side's
Art. 13(17) security-contact finding (Warning -> Info) while leaving the
other side untouched, and the JSON counts must equal a
`ComplianceChecker::with_sidecar()` computation — i.e. exactly what the
TUI renders.

   #[serde(skip)], so the primary machine-readable output had no stable rule
   identifier and consumers regexed the message. Violations now serialize
   both `rule_id` (stable internal key) and `sarif_rule_id` (registry-derived
   external id, same fallback as the SARIF renderer). Deserialization stays
   backward-compatible: old payloads default to SBOM-CRA-GENERAL, and known
   ids are mapped back to their registry &'static str keys so round-trips
   preserve rule identity (a derived impl would have forced 'de: 'static, so
   deserialization goes through an owned ViolationPayload mirror).

2. The five hand-maintained SARIF rule tables (ntia/fda/ssdf/eo14028/
   compliance, ~900 lines) are replaced by per-standard id slices next to
   the registry (NTIA/FDA/SSDF/EO14028/COMPLIANCE_SARIF_RULE_IDS) rendered
   through RuleMeta's new `name` + `short_description` fields (existing
   descriptor text harvested verbatim, so golden SARIF output is unchanged).
   Grouped SARIF ids that were table-only (SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-I, the AIACT/BSIAI
   cluster ids, SBOM-BSI-TR-03183-2-GENERAL) gained self-descriptor registry
   entries; aliased keys carry their canonical descriptor's text (enforced
   by test). complete_rule_catalogue stays as the safety net but now prefers
   registry identity over synthesis, so CNSA/PQC descriptors get real
   names/descriptions instead of "Compliance rule X". New all_rule_ids()
   enumeration is pinned to the match arms by a source-scanning test.
   Descriptor-metadata-only change: the dead SBOM-FDA-NAME descriptor (its
   results always surfaced as SBOM-FDA-GENERAL) is no longer declared.

3. The quality CLI no longer hand-builds SARIF with invented QUALITY-* rule
   ids. Non-AI profiles route through the new shared
   reports::generate_quality_sarif: compliance violations carry the exact
   same external rule ids as `validate -o sarif` (parity pinned by test),
   recommendations merge into the same run as advisory results under stable
   SBOM-QUALITY-REC-<CATEGORY> ids and are never level "error" (priority 1-2
   -> warning, else note), and score/grade/verdict ride on run-level
   properties (camelCase, consistent with the other SARIF runs; `compliant`
   added). quality -o json already embedded the serde ComplianceResult, so
   it picks up rule_id/sarif_rule_id from (1) unchanged.

4. OSCAL no longer flattens all standards into one anonymous assessment:
   one results[] entry per ComplianceResult with the standard name in
   title/description, props carrying standard id, is_compliant,
   applicability (+ reason), error/warning/info counts, and score; a
   satisfied/not-satisfied roll-up finding per applicable standard (clean
   runs keep their entry with a satisfied roll-up; N/A runs carry the
   verdict in props and get no roll-up). Observations now carry
   rule-id/sarif-rule-id props.

Machine-contract changes:
- JSON violations gain `rule_id` + `sarif_rule_id` (additive; golden JSON
  snapshot regenerated).
- quality -o sarif: ruleIds change from QUALITY-*/QUALITY-REC-* to registry
  ids / SBOM-QUALITY-REC-*; run properties move to camelCase
  (overallScore); a full rule catalogue is now declared; P1 recommendations
  demote from error to warning.
- OSCAL: per-standard results[] entries (previously one merged entry),
  roll-up findings precede violation findings.

Full `cargo test` green (1843 passed); `cargo clippy --all-features
--all-targets` warning count unchanged vs base; golden SARIF snapshot
byte-identical.

feat(parsers,model): purl-fallback ref resolution, doc_version capture, CDXA attestation ingestion

Three source-of-truth fixes in the parse/normalize layer.

purl-fallback ref resolution: real-world emitters (including this repo's
own demo fixtures) reference components by purl in dependencies[].ref /
dependsOn and vulnerabilities[].affects[].ref when components declare no
bom-ref. Those refs resolved against nothing, so edges and CVEs were
silently dropped -- the demo SBOM reported "no vulnerabilities" while its
own Source view listed a CVSS 9.8 entry. A secondary purl key map now
backs the bom-ref map; genuine bom-refs always win on collision.

doc_version: the CycloneDX top-level revision counter was deserialized
and thrown away. It is now captured on DocumentMetadata (additive,
skip_serializing_if), round-trips through convert (the emitter hardcoded
"version": 1, silently rewinding document history), and is available to
the diff engine.

CDXA attestation ingestion (phase 1): CycloneDX 1.6 `declarations`
(assessors, attestations, claims, evidence, affirmation, signatories) are
parsed into a normalized model gated on specVersion >= 1.6, with refLinks
resolved through the same id_map (bom-refs + purl fallback) and
unresolvable refs kept as Dangling so queries fail closed. Structural
verification only: signature PRESENCE is recorded, never cryptographically
verified, and the reported evidence level is capped accordingly. Attached
at FormatExtensions.declarations, so serialized output gains the key only
for documents that carry the section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(diff,quality): correct deviation scale, logical component identity, and vacuous readiness scores

BREAKING (JSON output semantics):

- diff-multi/timeline: deviation_scores and max_deviation are now 0-1
  fractions. They were 0-100 values that every consumer multiplied by 100
  again, rendering "Max Deviation: 10000.0%" and saturating every gauge
  and severity band.
- diff-multi/timeline: variable/inconsistent/divergent/evolution entries
  are keyed by version-stripped logical purl. A version bump counted as
  both an Added and a Removed component, so "Inconsistent: 20" exceeded
  the number of distinct components, and Timeline listed every upgrade
  twice.
- Diff JSON: ComponentChange gains component_type (additive, omitted when
  unset) resolved from CycloneDX type and refined for crypto assets
  (algorithm/certificate/protocol/key material) and ML (model/dataset).
- Diff JSON: metadata_changes gains doc_version entries. The demo pair
  moves from 15 to 18 total changes: two dependency edges that previously
  failed to resolve, plus the document revision bump.
- QualityDelta category names are profile-aware: CBOM pairs now report
  crypto category names and are scored under the CBOM profile, so the
  displayed categories reconcile with the score.

CryptographyMetrics::{quantum_readiness_score, pqc_readiness_score}
return Option<f32> (Rust API break for library consumers): they returned
a vacuous 100.0 for documents with zero algorithms, which is a perfect
score for having no cryptography at all. The CBOM scorer now
proportionally redistributes the PQC weight when absent, exactly as it
already did for vulnerability_score -- neither a free 100 nor a punitive
0. Renderers show "n/a".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tui): comprehensive UX overhaul across all modes for SBOM/CBOM/AI-BOM

Audit of every TUI mode against a 269-frame corpus (all tabs x profile x
80x24/120x40, plus overlays and interaction states) produced 203 findings;
30 survived adversarial verification and are fixed here, along with the
polish tail.

Honesty:
- Empty states no longer celebrate. "Great news! No known vulnerabilities"
  became a neutral, actionable message: absence of data is not proof of
  absence.
- Quantum readiness reads "n/a" instead of a full green 100% gauge when a
  document declares no cryptographic assets.
- The Graph tab distinguishes "no graph data" from "structure identical".
- Every key advertised in a shortcuts overlay or footer now exists in that
  context; keys that existed but were undiscoverable are documented.

Keyboard model (BREAKING for muscle memory):
- Digits always jump tabs. Components' security quick filters moved behind
  a 'Q' picker modal; Side-by-Side filters moved to A/r/m/x.
- 'e' is export everywhere: Dependencies fold moved to x/X, cycles to 'C'.
- View app: KEV filter k -> K, vulnerability group jump -> }/{ (its
  Tab binding was unreachable dead code behind the global tab switch).
- The threshold-tuning overlay, previously unreachable by any key, opens
  on 't'. Matrix 'D' is disabled with an explanation rather than opening a
  component modal on an SBOM name.
- View SBOM tab order aligns with the Diff app's digits.

Correctness:
- 'y' copies the item that is actually selected. Yank resolved through
  differently-sorted or unfiltered collections on Licenses, Vulnerabilities
  and all four CBOM asset tabs.
- CBOM verdicts come from one source of truth, so AES-128-ECB is not
  "quantum-safe" on one tab and FAIL on another.
- Multi-mode modals show their own keys, and the matrix pair-diff modal
  scrolls instead of silently truncating.

Layout:
- Quality, Compliance and AI-Readiness no longer collapse to empty borders
  at 80x24, the app's own advertised minimum: the headline score is always
  visible.
- Modal backgrounds use background_alt rather than the muted foreground
  color, which some terminals render as a light tan that made modal text
  nearly unreadable.
- Version tails elide instead of being overdrawn by the scrollbar, where
  "4.17.20 -> 4.17" read as a plausible wrong version.
- Hint bars drop whole hints with an ellipsis instead of clipping mid-word.

Also adds an env-gated frame-dump harness (TUI_FRAME_DUMP_DIR) that
renders every mode through the real event handlers for offline review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(compliance): registry-driven per-rule firing/silent matrix

FDA, SSDF, EO 14028, Standard and Comprehensive had essentially no
behavioral tests: nothing ever observed a passing verdict for them, and a
rule could stop firing without a single test noticing.

Each rule id in those standards now has a firing fixture (asserting the
violation surfaces at the registered severity) and a silent fixture,
built as minimal CycloneDX documents parsed through the real parser so
the tests exercise production normalization. The harness enforces
exhaustiveness in both directions: the entry table must equal the
standard's rule universe (skips carry a written reason), and no fixture
may emit a rule outside that universe, so a new check site forces a
matrix extension. Push-site severities that deviate from the registry
default are pinned explicitly.

Also adds the registry exhaustiveness test (every id resolves and belongs
to a SARIF slice or a documented sliceless list) and a CLI contract test
covering all 41 documented --standard spellings.

The harness itself was mutation-tested: a non-firing firing case and a
non-silent silent case both fail with clear diagnostics.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(compliance): CISA 2026, PCI DSS 6.3.2 and FSCT profiles; consume CDXA attestation evidence

Three new standards, each built from the primary source document rather
than recollection, with the citations recorded in the rule registry.

CISA 2026 Minimum Elements (--standard cisa-2026), 17 rules: the
finalized successor to the NTIA 2021 minimum elements, published
2026-07-29 by CISA/NSA/FBI and 15 international partners. Deliberately
stricter than the NTIA profile where the document is: a tool-only creator
list does not satisfy SBOM Author, and silent absence of a license fails
where an explicit no-assertion passes. Elements that a given format
cannot express (SPDX 2.x signatures, lifecycle phase) are
evidence-limited warnings, and requirements that survive normalization
unverifiably (RFC 9557 timestamp syntax) say so rather than claiming a
check.

PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 6.3.2 (--standard pci-dss), 12 rules: treats
the SBOM as the required inventory of bespoke, custom and third-party
components. A passing verdict is evidence that the inventory exists and
is usable for vulnerability management -- not a PCI compliance
certification, as the module documents. Thresholds we chose rather than
inherited (freshness) are labeled tool policy in the message itself.

CISA Framing Software Component Transparency, 3rd ed. (--standard fsct),
27 rules across the document's three maturity tiers, mapped to
Error/Warning/Info. Checks are format-gated where the evidence genuinely
cannot exist rather than failing documents for their format.

Attestation evidence is now consumed: a CDXA declaration that covers an
SSDF practice, a CRA conformity route, an EUCC certificate reference or
EO 14028 provenance satisfies the corresponding rule at structural or
signature-present level. Every pre-existing satisfaction path remains
valid as a self-declared fallback -- the guards only ever remove
violations -- and documents without declarations are unaffected. When
evidence fails the fail-closed gate, the violation message names the
reason (expired, countered, dangling reference, partial conformance)
instead of silently ignoring it.

Every new rule ships with firing and silent coverage in the per-rule
matrix.

fix(reports): honour --no-color/NO_COLOR for side-by-side output

The reporter factory takes a resolved `use_color` and honours it for the
Summary and Table arms, but the SideBySide arm dropped it and always
handed back a colored reporter. The reporter itself was never at fault:
it already had a `no_colors()` builder and routes all 73 of its emissions
through the `col()` gate -- the builder was simply never called.

`should_use_color(no_color)`, which folds together the flag, the NO_COLOR
convention and a stdout TTY check, wiring this one arm fixes all three at
once: escape sequences no longer pollute redirected or CI-captured
side-by-side output.

is escape-free when use_color is false (and that side-by-side still
colors when it is true, so the fix cannot silently disable color), plus
CLI contract tests for --no-color and NO_COLOR=1 that assert on real
rendered content so they cannot pass vacuously. All three fail without
the one-line change.

fix(tui): honour --no-color, and treat empty NO_COLOR as unset

Same defect class as the side-by-side reporter, one layer deeper: the
TUI resolved its startup theme from `std::env::var_os("NO_COLOR")` alone,
so the `--no-color` flag never reached it. `sbom-tools diff a b
--no-color` launched a fully colored TUI, as did the view, diff-multi,
timeline and matrix TUIs.

`startup_theme` now takes the resolved flag, and `run_tui`/`run_view_tui`
thread it from `config.output.no_color` at all five launch sites
(BREAKING: both entry points gain a `no_color` parameter). The flag is
passed explicitly rather than stashed in a global so the behaviour is
testable and the data flow is visible.

Also aligns the environment check with the NO_COLOR convention and with
the rest of the CLI: the variable counts only when present AND non-empty.
The TUI used `is_some()`, so `NO_COLOR=` forced a monochrome TUI while
logs and reports — which use `is_none_or(|v| v.is_empty())` — stayed
colored. One invocation could not be consistent with itself.

Monochrome remains sticky under the `T` toggle, so a user who asked for
no color cannot be cycled back into a colored theme; a test pins that.

Verified end to end in a pseudo-terminal, counting SGR hue codes in what
the TUI actually paints: `--no-color` 0 vs 7 by default, `NO_COLOR=1` 0,
and `NO_COLOR=` (empty) correctly still colored. Both new unit tests fail

TUI UX overhaul, engine correctness fixes, and compliance P3–P4

fix(cli,diff): honest multi-SBOM format list, labelled timeline pairs, pinned similarity scales

Three findings from validating the timeline and fleet commands.

**--help advertised formats these commands reject.** `diff-multi`,
`timeline` and `matrix` offered the full ReportFormat list, but they have
no summary/markdown/SARIF renderer, so those values parsed fine and then
died at runtime with exit 3 after every SBOM had been read. They now take
a restricted value enum: `--help` lists only auto/tui/json, and a bad
value is a clap usage error (exit 2) naming the real choices. The runtime
gate in cli::multi stays as defense in depth, since a format can also
arrive from the config file. Two tests that pinned the old runtime
message now pin the improved contract.

**Timeline diffs carried no pair identity.** `incremental_diffs` and
`cumulative_from_first` are bare `DiffResult` arrays, so a JSON consumer
could only infer which pair each entry described from its position and
the documented ordering. Adds index-aligned `incremental_pairs` and
`cumulative_pairs` (from/to index and display name). Additive and
`#[serde(default)]`, so existing consumers are unaffected.

**Similarity was reported in two scales.** Matrix emits `similarity_scores`
as a 0-1 fraction while the embedded per-pair `DiffResult.semantic_score`
is 0-100 — the same metric, since similarity is literally
`semantic_score / 100`. Neither value is wrong and changing either would
break a real contract: the 0-100 scale is shared with single `diff`
everywhere, and the 0-1 fractions are what the multi layer uses for
deviation. So the scales are now stated explicitly in the doc comments of
all three fields, and a test pins the relationships
(`similarity == semantic_score / 100`, `deviation == 1 - similarity`)
so they cannot drift apart silently again, which has happened once.

fix(tui): stop the shortcuts overlay contradicting its own This-Tab section

Writing a verified keyboard reference from the handlers surfaced four
Global/Navigation rows that are false on specific tabs, two of which
contradicted the This-Tab section rendered directly above them in the
same frame:

- `l  Color legend` — Compliance binds `l` to next-standard and Source to
  expand/scroll-right, so those tabs consume it first.
- `h/l  Collapse/expand (tree tabs)` — true only on Source; Dependencies
  binds `h` to change highlighting, and Compliance to switch standards,
  which the overlay separately (and correctly) lists.
- `K  Keyboard shortcuts` — Side-by-Side binds `K` to scrolling, and its
  own This-Tab section says so. (`?` and F1 still open the overlay.)
- `g/G  First/Last` — Licenses, Vulnerabilities and Compliance bind `g`
  to grouping.

The dispatcher gives the active tab first refusal on every key, so a
global row is only true where no tab handler consumes it. Rather than
thread `TabKind` in and maintain a per-tab exclusion table — which would
rot exactly like the hints this audit has been removing — the overlay now
subtracts the keys the active tab already advertises. `tab_items` is the
tab's own `ViewState::shortcuts()`, the same source the footer renders,
so binding a key in a tab makes the shadowed global row disappear on its
own with no second place to update.

Rows advertising several keys keep the ones still free: with Components
active, `y/Ctrl+C  Copy selected` renders as `Ctrl+C  Copy selected`
because the tab binds `y`, and `j/k` moves to the This-Tab section. Rows
are dropped only when the tab claims every key, and with no tab context
(multi modes) nothing changes at all.

No key stops working and none becomes undocumented — each moves to the
section that describes what it actually does there.

fix(cli,tui): reject sbomqs-json outside quality, honour empty NO_COLOR, bind advertised `g`

Three defects surfaced while verifying documentation claims against the
binary — each a case of the tool doing something other than what it said.

`diff` and `view` accepted `-o sbomqs-json` and silently emitted ordinary
diff/view JSON, because the format fell through to the JSON reporter.
The caller asked for one format and got another, which is exactly what
the `oscal-json` guard immediately above was written to prevent ("reject
it up front instead of silently emitting plain JSON"). Both now bail with
a pointer to `quality -o sbomqs-json`, matching that precedent and its
exit code.

`should_use_color()` used `var("NO_COLOR").is_err()`, treating an empty
`NO_COLOR=` as set. Per the convention the variable counts only when
present AND non-empty, which the log setup and the TUI theme already do —
so a single invocation stripped colour from reports while keeping it in
logs and the TUI. This corrects an overstatement in f3a9445, whose
message claimed the TUI had been aligned with "the rest of the CLI": it
was aligned with the log path, not the report path. Its unit test was
re-deriving the old rule rather than the documented one, so it would have
agreed with either implementation; it now mirrors the convention.

The Graph Changes tab advertised `g/G  First/Last` in its footer and in
the `?` overlay, but bound only `Home` and `End`/`G`. `g` fell through to
the global `select_first`, which has no arm for that tab, so it silently
did nothing. `g` is now bound alongside `Home`, with a behavioural test
that fails if the binding is dropped again.
